title: Board card menu stays open and its full-page backdrop stays live after keyboard focus tabs out of it
why: Blocks keyboard-only and screen-reader users: the card's primary action menu never closes on Tab, leaving a stale, still-interactive overlay covering the whole page while focus visibly moves elsewhere.
detail: Live-reproduced with Playwright: open a card's "..." menu with Enter, then press Tab repeatedly. Focus correctly advances through the 5 menuitems and then out to <body> and on to the app's top-nav icon, but at every step `document.querySelector('[role="menu"]')` and `.zui-cardmenu-backdrop` are still present and visibly rendered (verified via getComputedStyle). The component closes only on Escape or a mouse click on the backdrop (CardMenu.tsx:131-137, :183); there is no blur/focusout handler. This breaks the WAI-ARIA menu-button pattern, which requires Tab to dismiss the menu, and leaves an invisible full-viewport click-catcher (`.zui-cardmenu-backdrop`, position: fixed) live over the rest of the page — the next accidental click anywhere just closes the stale menu instead of hitting the control the user meant to activate. Fix: close the menu (call `close()`) on the popup's onBlur when focus leaves it, or run a `focusout` listener that checks `relatedTarget` against the popup subtree.

title: Board search input's replacement focus indicator reuses the exact gold that already failed the project's own 3:1 non-text-contrast bar
why: Keyboard users tabbing to the board's search field get no adequately visible focus indicator — fails WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast for the one control most people reach first on the board.
detail: Live-measured via getComputedStyle after focusing `.board-bar .search`: `outline-style: none` on the input, and the wrapping `.board-bar` gets `border-color: rgb(214, 164, 65)` (raw `--accent`) plus `box-shadow: rgba(214, 164, 65, 0.1) 0 0 0 2px`. `--accent` (#d6a441) measures 2.27:1 on white and 2.03:1 on the paper `--bg` — the identical numbers `src/index.css:343-349` cites as the reason the global `:focus-visible` ring uses `--accent-ink` (#836427, 4.9-5.5:1) instead. This one control has its own hand-rolled `:focus-within` style (added for #447 to move focus off the native outline onto the wrapping pill) and was never updated to the accent-ink fix that shipped everywhere else. Swap `border-color: var(--accent)` for `var(--accent-ink)` on `.board-bar:focus-within`.

title: Stage-change and CV-variant-delete buttons measure under the 24px target-size floor for mouse/stylus pointers
why: WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is not touch-specific; anyone using a mouse, trackpad, or a switch/head-pointer on a laptop hits an ~88x20px stage-change control and a ~13x21px delete button.
detail: axe-core (wcag22aa `target-size`, impact "serious") flags 8 nodes on /board/9001 desktop (`.detail-rail-step`, e.g. "Interested") and 1 node each on /cv desktop and mobile (`.cv-rail-del`, "Delete variant …"). Both controls do carry a documented touch-size fix — `@media (pointer: coarse) { .detail-rail-step, .stage-chip { min-height: 44px } }` (App.css:5866) and an equivalent 44px overlay for `.cv-rail-del` (cv.css:189) — but 2.5.8's 24px floor applies to any pointer input, not only touch, so the un-fixed default size still fails for a plain mouse. Add an unconditional `min-height: 24px` (not just inside `pointer: coarse`) to both selectors.

title: Every route overflows horizontally at 320px width + 200% text zoom, driven by the fixed-width top-bar icon buttons
where: src/App.css:31-45 (.top, grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr), :62-70 (.top-icon, width/height: 38px, flex: none); all 9 routes tested
why: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow: a low-vision user zoomed to 200% on a 320px phone gets a page that scrolls sideways on every screen in the app, not just one.
detail: Measured live (Playwright, viewport 320x700, `document.documentElement.style.fontSize = '200%'` applied via `page.evaluate` after `goto` — not `addInitScript`, which fires before `documentElement` exists and would silently no-op). All 9 routes tested (`/`, `/board`, `/board/9001`, `/feed`, `/insights`, `/companies`, `/people`, `/cv`, `/settings`) show `scrollWidth > clientWidth` (332-374px content in a 320px viewport). The one element overflowing on nearly every route is `.top-icon` inside `.top-corner.end`: it's a fixed 38x38px circle with `flex: none` sitting in a `1fr auto 1fr` grid track that, unlike `.bottombar` (App.css:645, already fixed with `minmax(0, 1fr)` for this exact reason, per its own comment), has no `minmax(0, …)` floor. `.top`'s grid tracks need the same `minmax(0, 1fr)` treatment `.bottombar` already got.

title: Unwrapped long text (rail labels, company names, funnel bar) adds further overflow at 320px/200% zoom on top of the top-bar issue
why: Independent of the top-bar bug, several pages overflow further because specific long strings (CV variant labels, a company name, a dashboard chart bar) don't wrap or truncate at large text sizes — a second, page-specific WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow cause.
detail: Same live 320px/200%-zoom sweep, isolating offending elements by `getBoundingClientRect()`. `/` overflows to 623px (worst of all routes) because of `.stage-offer`/`.today-ascent-bar` chart rows on the dashboard's "Moved this week" list; `/cv` reaches 374px from `.cv-rail-step`/`.cv-rail-row` (variant names in the left rail); `/board/9001` reaches 357px from `.detail-pill-co` (the company name pill on the detail header). These are separate from the top-bar grid issue and need per-component wrapping/truncation (`min-width: 0` on the flex/grid item plus `text-overflow: ellipsis` or `overflow-wrap: anywhere`) rather than one shared fix.

title: Read-only fit-score star rating announces its value in hardcoded English regardless of the active locale
where: src/components/StarRating.tsx:44 (aria-label={ariaLabel ?? `${value ?? 0} of ${max}`}); callers src/board.tsx:168 and src/dashboard.tsx:642 pass no aria-label
why: Dutch-locale screen-reader users hear "4 of 5" in English on every board card and every dashboard "Next up" row with a fit score — the one string in this component that bypassed i18next entirely.
detail: `StarRating`'s read-only branch falls back to a literal template string, `${value ?? 0} of ${max}`, whenever no `aria-label` prop is supplied (StarRating.tsx:44). Both call sites that render it read-only — `board.tsx:168` and `dashboard.tsx:642` — call `<StarRating value={a.fit_score} readOnly />` with no `aria-label`, so this fallback is what a screen reader announces in production for every fit-score chip, in both `en` and `nl`. This violates the project's own locked rule ("strict key parity… externalize all user-facing strings") and WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts, since the string's real language never matches `<html lang>` in the `nl` locale and isn't marked. Fix: give the two call sites a translated `aria-label` (e.g. `t("detail.fitScoreLabel", { value, max })`), matching the pattern already used for `starLabel` elsewhere.

title: Generated CV/cover-letter/offer PDFs carry no accessibility tagging
where: src/pdf.ts:77 (generateCvPdf), :256, :360 (other jsPDF documents) — no setLanguage/tag-tree calls anywhere in the file
why: A job-seeker who is a screen-reader user cannot verify their own exported CV, and a hiring pipeline running its own accessibility check on submitted documents will flag the file.
detail: `generateCvPdf` and the other document generators build the PDF purely via jsPDF's positional text/drawing calls (`doc.text`, `doc.rect`, …), with no call to set a document language, no structure/tag tree, and no reading-order metadata — the file has none of the markers a screen reader or a PDF/UA checker looks for, which matches jsPDF's default (untagged) output. This is speculative in the sense that it wasn't verified by opening the output in a real screen reader, but the absence of any tagging code combined with jsPDF's documented behavior makes it a near-certain gap. Given the product's own two-column CV layout (`--doc-aside` sidebar + main column), an untagged PDF's implicit reading order is also likely to interleave the two columns incorrectly for any assistive reader. Full remediation (PDF/UA tagging) is a larger lift than this pass covers — flagging so it can be scoped.

title: Quick-add's disabled "Add" buttons give no accessible reason for being unavailable
where: src/components/QuickAddDialog.tsx:214-219 (required title input, no visible/programmatic required indicator beyond the bare label), :244-249 (disabled={busy || !title.trim()} with no aria-describedby)
why: A keyboard/screen-reader user who tabs to "Add & open" before typing a title just hears "button, dimmed" with no explanation of what to fix.
detail: The dialog prevents an invalid submit structurally — both submit buttons are `disabled` while `!title.trim()` — which avoids a true WCAG 3.3.1 error-identification failure (there is never an actual failed-validation state to announce), but it trades that for a silently-inert control: nothing on the button or the title field communicates *why* it won't activate. A native browser validation message (removing `disabled` and letting `required` + form submission trigger `:invalid` UI) or an `aria-describedby` pointing at a short hint ("Enter a title first") would give the same protection with an accessible explanation.

title: No formal WCAG conformance target is committed, and closing the gap from here is a real, scoped cost — not a rounding error
where: CLAUDE.md "No formal WCAG conformance target committed (undecided)"; scope basis: this audit's 9 findings above plus src/index.css, src/App.css, src/pdf.ts
why: Product/roadmap decision-makers need a real cost estimate, not a vague "we should be accessible" — this is that estimate, grounded in what this audit actually found.
detail: The good news first: axe-core across all 10 routes at 2 viewports (wcag2a/2aa/21aa/22aa) returned exactly one rule id in violation — target-size — for 10 nodes total, and manual review found the tablist/tabpanel wiring, focus-trap, toast live-region, and heading/landmark structure all correctly built (recent fixes #447/#496-502/#535/#656 clearly did real work). The real cost of committing to AA is concentrated in a handful of specific, fixable gaps: the CardMenu focus/blur bug (M), the search-focus contrast regression (S), two target-size spots (S), the top-bar reflow grid (M), page-specific reflow overflows (M), the StarRating i18n leak (S), and PDF tagging if the org decides exported documents must conform too (L, and arguably out of scope for a *web* AA conformance statement). Rough total: 2-3 focused days of engineering plus one design-side decision (whether exported PDFs are in scope), not a rewrite — the architecture (design tokens, a shared Dialog/focus-trap, a shared TabBar/PillTabs, axe already wired as a devDependency) already does most of the heavy lifting a conformance statement would need.

title: Applications created via the browser extension never get a status_history row
why: every downstream funnel/response/conversion metric keys off status_history, so extension-sourced applications are invisible to all of them
detail: POST /api/v1/applications (the route "the browser extension uses", per its own comment) inserts directly into applications with status='interested' but has no matching `INSERT INTO status_history`, unlike every other creation path (POST /api/applications:754, worker/feed.ts:628, worker/demo.ts). funnelReachCounts, responseRate and responseTime in src/stats.ts all derive solely from status_history, so an application added by the extension — a positioning-claim feature ("the pipeline carries its origin") — contributes 0 to the funnel's own base count until some later status_history-writing transition happens to it. The fix is one INSERT alongside the existing one, matching the pattern already used everywhere else.

title: Public share page's momentum verdict is a stale copy missing the small-n floor the in-app version was fixed to have
why: the exact overconfident-verdict bug that was deliberately fixed in-app (MOMENTUM_MIN_EVENTS) was never fixed on the one surface a stranger actually sees
detail: src/format.ts's computePipelineMomentum has a documented guard: below MOMENTUM_MIN_EVENTS=6 combined recent+prior forward moves, the verdict is 'early' rather than up/down/flat, with a comment explaining that at prior=1 a single extra move used to read as +100% "speeding up" off the least possible evidence. worker/index.ts's /shared/:token handler reimplements the identical recentMoves/priorMoves ratio inline (lines 1991-2036) but never carries that guard forward — `else if (priorMoves === 0) momentum = S.faster` fires on a single stage advance. A user with two forward moves total can have their public share link tell an outside viewer "Moving faster" with the same confidence the in-app version was rewritten specifically to avoid.

title: "Ghost rate" is a named positioning metric that is never actually computed as a rate anywhere
where: src/stats.ts (no ghost-rate function); PRODUCT.md Product Purpose
why: the product's #1 claim ("Zenith diagnoses where the search is failing") explicitly lists ghost rate among the computed diagnostics, but no code computes it
detail: grep across src/ and worker/ turns up 'ghosted' only as a status value, a manual one-tap action (dashboard.tsx:474 markNoReply) and a bucket of outcome-reason labels inside outcomeBreakdown — never as an aggregate fraction (e.g. "38% of closed applications ended in silence"). Response rate, time-in-stage and the conversion funnel each got a dedicated, carefully n-gated function in src/stats.ts; ghost rate got none, despite the same input (status_history + outcome_reason) already supporting it. A user reading Insights currently has to eyeball the outcome-breakdown bar chart and do the division themselves.

title: outcomeBreakdown splits "never heard back" across two unrelated-looking bars instead of unifying it
why: the distinction the brief specifically asks about — "no reply ever" vs "rejected after screening" — is captured in the data but not surfaced as one number
detail: OUTCOME_REASONS defines rejected:'no_response' (labelled "No response") and ghosted:'no_reply_after_applying' (labelled "No reply after applying") as two semantically-identical-but-differently-slugged reasons under two different terminal statuses. outcomeBreakdown tallies by raw reason string, so these appear as two separate bars in the Insights outcome chart rather than one "never got a response at all" figure — understating the single most diagnostic number a job-search tracker can report (total silence rate) by splitting it in half.

title: Median time-in-stage is only implemented for one stage (applied); the rest of the funnel has no duration metric
why: PRODUCT.md's Product Purpose names "median time-in-stage" generically, but only applied->next-move (responseTime) and applied->offer (medianTimeToOffer) exist; screening and interview have no duration metric at all
detail: The original medianTimeInStageDays was correctly removed for mixing censored (still-open) and completed durations into one biased median — a real, well-reasoned fix, documented in the comment at stats.ts:91. But nothing replaced it for the screening and interview stages specifically; a user cannot see "interviews typically run 12 days before a decision" anywhere, only "how long until the first reply" and "how long from apply to offer". The correct shape to extend (median over completed transitions of that specific from->to pair, count still open reported alongside) is already written once in responseTime — it needs generalizing per-stage-pair, not reinventing.

title: Application source (feed channel vs extension vs manual) is recorded but never used to compute conversion by channel
where: migrations/0001_init.sql:30 (applications.source); worker/feed.ts:164,215,255 (source values); src/stats.ts (no source-keyed metric)
why: positioning claim #2 ("sourcing and pipeline are one loop") implies the loop feeds diagnostics, but the source column that would prove which channel actually works is write-only
detail: applications.source is populated with distinguishable values ('feed:adzuna', 'feed:greenhouse', 'feed:ashby', 'extension', or left null for hand-typed entries — see worker/public-api.ts:414 and worker/feed.ts:620) but responseRate, funnelConversions and outcomeBreakdown all operate on the whole account with no source dimension. A user with ~50 applications across several channels currently cannot learn "Adzuna listings convert at 2x the rate of cold applications from the company site" even though every row needed for that answer already exists — this is exactly the diagnostic question status_history + source together already support and nothing reads.

title: Logged interactions are never correlated with whether they change outcomes
where: migrations/0006_contact_interactions.sql (interactions table); worker/index.ts:1514 /api/stats returns interactions; src/insights.tsx (no follow-up-effect metric)
why: interactions carry a timestamp per application and status_history carries stage-change timestamps for the same application, so "did a follow-up precede the next forward move" is answerable from data already collected and shipped to the client on every /api/stats call
detail: /api/stats already joins in a per-application 'last interaction' query (worker/index.ts:1514, used today only for the board's "gone quiet" badge). A join against status_history could answer whether applications that got a logged nudge before N days idle in a stage subsequently advanced at a higher rate than ones that didn't — the single most actionable insight a job-seeker could get ("following up works" or "it doesn't, stop wasting time on it"), and it needs no new column, only a new computation over rows that ship to the browser already.

title: Demo seed data can produce an application invisible to the funnel's own base count
why: the demo seeder itself demonstrates the exact status_history gap pattern that would silently corrupt real-account metrics if a real transition skipped intermediate stages the same way
detail: The hand-crafted 'ghosted' demo application inserts a single status_history row `(NULL, 'ghosted')`, skipping 'interested'/'applied' entirely — unlike the bulk demo applications a few lines below (historyFor(), line 247), which correctly synthesize a full stage-by-stage trail even for terminal outcomes. Because FUNNEL_STAGES in src/stats.ts excludes 'ghosted', reachedIndexByApp (stats.ts:27-36) finds no matching to_status for this application and it contributes 0 to funnelReachCounts — including counts[0], the "total that ever entered the pipeline" figure the Insights funnel card headlines with (insights.tsx:301). The demo account's own funnel base undercounts by one for exactly the reason the code comments elsewhere warn about.

title: Insights never states the sample size behind the momentum verdict, only behind the KPI band
why: the response-rate and time-to-offer tiles both show or gate on n, but the momentum band's verdict text never surfaces recent/prior counts even though the function already returns them
detail: computePipelineMomentum returns {verdict, recent, prior} and the 'early' verdict already exists for the sub-MOMENTUM_MIN_EVENTS case, but once past that floor the rendered detail (t('stats.momentumDetail', {count: pipe.recent, recent: pipe.recent, prior: pipe.prior})) states the two raw counts in prose rather than as a labelled n — a user has to parse a sentence to find the sample size behind "up"/"down", where the KPI tiles beside it show n directly as '{responded}/{applied}' or a 'from N offers' subline. Minor relative to the other findings, but the same honesty pattern applied inconsistently on the same screen.

title: Board card company chip hard-clips mid-word — ellipsis rule is inert
why: text-overflow: ellipsis never applies to a display:flex container, so every company cell cuts mid-word with no signal.
detail: Every board card shows it: 'SOLACE SYSTEMS · DIE', 'BRIGHTPATH TALENT P', 'FIELDSTONE ANALYTIC', 'NORTHWIND CLOUD · M'. The rule at App.css:5548 sets overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis on .bstrip > span, but the same rule makes the span display:flex, and ellipsis only renders on a block container with inline content. Wrap the text in an inner block (or drop the flex and centre with line-height) so the existing ellipsis declaration actually fires. The title attribute already carries the full string, so only the visual clip needs fixing.

title: Detail page stage selector reads as scattered labels, not a control
where: detail-desktop.png / detail-mobile.png (stage block top-right) · src/detail.tsx:330-337 + src/App.css:929 (.detail-rail-step)
why: Seven bare small-caps words in a loose two-column block (three ragged lines on mobile), live stages and terminal outcomes mixed at equal weight, only the current one has any shape.
detail: INTERESTED/APPLIED/SCREENING/INTERVIEW/OFFER are an ordered pipeline, but the layout gives no order and no affordance — REJECTED/WITHDRAWN/GHOSTED interleave with them in a second column on desktop and wrap arbitrarily on mobile. The current-stage ink fill (allowed) is the only visible element, so the rest look like static metadata rather than the app's most important state control. Lay the five live stages as one ordered rail (quiet ring per step, ink fill for current — both within the locked palette rules) and set the three outcomes apart as a visually distinct 'ended' cluster below it.

title: Persistent focus ring boxed around the detail page job title
where: detail-desktop.png / detail-mobile.png (outline around 'Senior Platform Engineer') · src/detail.tsx:152 + src/index.css:348
why: Programmatic focus on the h2 paints the global 2px brass outline around a non-interactive heading on every card open.
detail: detail.tsx:152 moves focus to the title heading (good a11y), but the global focus style from index.css:348 draws its 2px --accent-ink outline there, so the first thing the reader sees is a stray box around the job title — it reads as a broken editable field. Keep the focus move, suppress the ring on this heading only (it is not an interactive target, so hiding its outline costs nothing): a scoped outline:none on the tabindex=-1 heading, or a :focus-visible-only rule if the global one currently matches plain :focus.

title: Feed spends the gold accent on everything — the real primary loses
where: feed-desktop.png / feed-mobile.png · src/feed.tsx:761 ('Check now') vs :1206 ('Add to pipeline')
why: Two gold-filled primaries per screen plus gold chips, gold match meters, gold card border — accent stops meaning 'act here'.
detail: 'Check now' (a maintenance refresh) is a filled primary at the top while 'Add to pipeline' (the action the screen exists for) is a filled primary in the card — same weight, and the selected sort/min-fit chips, skill chips, match meters and the focused card's border are all the same gold. One filled accent per screen: demote 'Check now' to secondary, let selected chips carry a tint instead of the full accent outline, and the add button becomes the unambiguous focal point. This also stops the accent gold reading as the OFFER stage family everywhere at once.

title: Companies list: raw URLs as body text, and near-empty rows break the rhythm
why: Rows print the full https://… string at ink weight while name-only rows (Alderly Health, Meridian Cloud, Ridgeline) collapse to thin empty cards.
detail: companies.tsx:190 renders c.website verbatim, so half the rows carry a second line of protocol noise and the other half have no second line at all — the list alternates between two card heights with no shared rhythm. Strip to the bare domain in muted text (the href keeps the full URL), and give every row one consistent meta line — e.g. open-application count or last-touch — so sparse companies look sparse by content, not unfinished by layout.

title: People rows: outreach pill floats to a different spot on every row
why: The status pill sits inline after the email and wraps unpredictably — Owen's drops to its own line, others sit beside the address at varying offsets — so five rows never scan as a column.
detail: Status is the one thing the 'Owe a reply' section sorts by, yet it has no fixed slot: it trails the email wherever the line breaks. Pin the pill to a consistent position (e.g. right-aligned on the email line, under the role text) so the eye can run down one rail of statuses. Secondary: the pill's lowercase monospace-in-a-grey-box styling reads as debug output next to the designed chips elsewhere — the small-caps eyebrow treatment used across the app would match.

title: Insights desktop ends in a giant empty month grid
where: insights-desktop.png (September calendar) · src/insights.tsx:524 + src/calendar.tsx (CalendarTab month grid)
why: A full six-week calendar with zero events is the largest element on the page, beside a note that admits 'Nothing scheduled ahead — 8 items are in the past.'
detail: The emptiest content gets the most pixels. Mobile already solves this — below 900px insights renders a 'Show calendar' button instead (insights.tsx:95). Apply the same judgement on desktop when there are no upcoming events: show the 'nothing ahead' note plus the most recent past events and a control to expand the grid. The grid earns its space the week it has something to show.

title: Insights 'Activity' section is a ruled heading over a lone centered button
why: A full section header whose entire body is one button looks unfinished next to the designed panels above it.
detail: Every other section on Insights leads with content; this one leads with chrome. Either seed it with the last two or three activity entries and let the button become 'Show all', or drop the ruled header and fold the label into the button itself. Same applies to the mobile 'CALENDAR → Show calendar' pair, which at least has the excuse of hiding a heavy widget.

title: Overview: the Gone-quiet rail competes with 'Next up' at equal weight
why: Four white cards with four full 'Archive' buttons sit beside the task list at identical card weight, splitting the page's single job — the next action.
detail: The product brief says success is knowing the next action within seconds. The left column earns the focus (hero count, due list), but the right rail answers a housekeeping question with the same surface, radius and button treatment, so the eye ping-pongs. Compress gone-quiet to single-line rows with a quiet text action (the copy already says 'when you're ready' — the design should whisper too), keeping the archive affordance one click away without four filled-white cards' worth of weight.

title: '0 sent' hero digit beside an active-looking sparkline
why: A hero-sized serif zero is emphasis spent on nothing, and the gold history bars right beside it read as 'activity' at a glance.
detail: The panel sets '0 sent' at headline size while the sparkline shows past weeks' bars — two signals that contradict each other until read closely. When the weekly count is zero, drop to the muted-sentence register the app already uses ('Nothing sent yet this week') and let the sparkline carry the history; save the big number for a week that has one.

title: Board mobile stage strip clips mid-label with no scroll cue
where: board-mobile.png ('INTERV…' cut at the right edge) · src/App.css:2662 (board overflow-x band)
why: The fourth tab is sliced exactly at 'INTERV' with a hard edge — it reads as broken rendering rather than 'more to the right'.
detail: The strip scrolls, but a hard clip on a monospace caps label looks like the truncation bug on the cards below it. The board columns already have edge-fade machinery in App.css (~2824); give the tab strip the same soft fade (or a few px of right padding so a partial chip shows with breathing room) so the affordance reads as intentional. Verify against the live render — full-page capture can exaggerate the edge.

title: Admin users: row actions visually detached from the account they act on
where: admin-desktop.png / admin-mobile.png (Reset password / Remove below both users) · src/settings/admin.tsx:95-117
why: Two account rows, then one Reset password / Remove pair floating below both — nothing ties the destructive 'Remove' to a specific user.
detail: The code maps buttons per user (admin.tsx:95-117, with per-user aria-labels), but the rendered spacing puts the pair on its own line under the second row where it scans as card-level. With more invitees this gets worse. Put each row's actions on the row itself, right-aligned, and let 'Remove' keep its red only there — a destructive control should never be ambiguous about its target even for a second.

title: Native checkboxes break the control register on Settings and Prep
where: settings-desktop.png (Single-key shortcuts row) + detail-desktop.png (Interview prep list) · src/index.css:336-339 (accent-color)
why: Every other control is designed; the raw OS checkbox (accent-tinted) is the one off-register element, and on Settings it also breaks the row's label/value column pattern.
detail: index.css deliberately leans on accent-color — a fine lazy default — but on the Settings general panel five rows show small-caps values on the right and the sixth ends in a bare checkbox, so the column rhythm snaps. Minimum fix without owning a checkbox component: size it consistently and align it to the same right rail as the small-caps values; the prep list can keep native boxes since they sit inside a task idiom where they read fine.

title: README claims three themes; app is light-only
why: README's own feature list contradicts a locked product decision documented two files over
detail: README.md's 'Everywhere' section says 'Three themes (Automatic / Light / Dark)'. CLAUDE.md and PRODUCT.md both state Light-only was shipped with the #535 fizzy-shell work (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-fizzy-shell-design.md) and that no data-theme attribute or prefers-color-scheme branch exists anywhere in the CSS — confirmed by grep, zero hits in src/. Anyone reading only the README believes a removed feature still exists.

title: /api/v1 documented as read-only in three files, but has a write endpoint
why: Security-relevant claim about a Bearer-key surface is wrong in README, CLAUDE.md, and PRODUCT.md alike
detail: README.md ('Read-only REST API (`/api/v1`...)'), CLAUDE.md:10 ('/api/v1/* (read-only Bearer key)') and PRODUCT.md:38 ('a read-only /api/v1 key') all describe the surface as read-only. `api.post("/applications", ...)` at worker/public-api.ts:381 is a genuine write path (find-or-create company, INSERT into applications) added for the browser extension (#477). A reader deciding whether it's safe to hand an API key to a browser extension is told the wrong threat model.

title: SELF_HOSTING.md never mentions RESEND_API_KEY
why: A required secret for a shipped, cron-triggered feature (weekly digest) is entirely absent from the self-hosting walkthrough
detail: worker/email/index.ts:15-16 gates all outbound email on `env.RESEND_API_KEY`, and wrangler.jsonc schedules a Monday 08:00 weekly-digest cron. SELF_HOSTING.md's 'Set secrets' section documents BETTER_AUTH_SECRET/URL, ADZUNA_APP_ID/KEY, and the three VAPID secrets, but RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM appear nowhere in the file. A self-hoster gets no digest email and no explanation why — the docs describe every other optional secret's silent-skip behavior except this one.

title: Forwarded-email logging requires Cloudflare Email Routing setup, documented nowhere
why: A shipped inbound-mail feature has zero setup instructions for the infrastructure it depends on
detail: The exported `email()` handler (worker/index.ts:2691) only fires if the self-hoster has configured Cloudflare Email Routing to forward a mailbox to this Worker — a dashboard step outside wrangler.jsonc entirely. Neither README.md nor SELF_HOSTING.md mentions Email Routing, a catch-all/specific address, or that this feature (worker/forwarded-email.ts) exists at all. A self-hoster has no way to discover or enable it from the docs.

title: Browser extension is undiscoverable outside its own folder
why: A complete, well-written install guide exists but nothing points a user to it
detail: extension/README.md is thorough (load-unpacked steps, options, autofill, exact POST/GET routes used). But README.md and SELF_HOSTING.md never mention `extension/` exists, and unlike the bookmarklet — which gets its own in-app Settings section (src/settings/bookmarklet-section.tsx) — there is no in-app link, card, or mention of the extension anywhere in src/settings/. A user would have to browse the repo tree to find it.

title: HANDOFF.md presents the screenshot rig as byte-stable; it now hard-fails
why: CLAUDE.md points every UI change at this rig as the pixel-diff gate, and the durable record backing it is now describing a tool that doesn't run
detail: HANDOFF.md:88-90 states 'Prove the harness is byte-stable before trusting any diff... Two full runs into different OUT_DIRs must differ on 0 of 52 captures' and 'A non-zero line is a real defect' (line 359). scripts/screenshot-baseline.mjs:47 clicks `.top-add`, a selector with zero matches anywhere in src/ (confirmed by grep — only a stray comment in Button.tsx references the old class name). The harness hard-fails at capture 3 of 52. HANDOFF.md, the file CLAUDE.md cites as the durable record of this rig, gives no indication it is currently non-functional.

title: CLAUDE.md's cv.tsx split claim overstates what happened
why: Grouping cv.tsx with settings.tsx/network.tsx as 'since split' implies a clean move that didn't happen for cv.tsx
detail: CLAUDE.md's editing-conventions note lists settings.tsx→src/settings/, network.tsx→companies.tsx/contacts.tsx, and cv.tsx→src/cv/ together as files that 'have since been split.' The first two are accurate (no settings.tsx or network.tsx remain at src/ top level). But src/cv.tsx (15.4K, the CVTab component) still exists alongside the src/cv/ directory — it imports from src/cv/tailor.tsx, src/cv/sections.tsx etc. rather than having moved into it. The phrasing invites a reader to expect cv.tsx is gone the way network.tsx is.

title: In-app API reference documents 2 of 4 available /api/v1 endpoints
why: The one in-app place a user learns what their API key can do omits the endpoint the extension actually relies on
detail: The `ApiDocs` component (src/settings/api.tsx:245) lists only `GET /applications` and `GET /applications/:id`. worker/public-api.ts also exposes `POST /applications` (:381, the extension's save-to-pipeline write) and `GET /profile` (:427, contact-basics for autofill) under the same Bearer key. A user reading Settings to understand their own key's blast radius doesn't learn it can create records or read their profile.

title: README project-layout block lists files that no longer exist
why: The layout diagram is meant as an orientation map for a first-time reader and misnames the actual module split
detail: README.md's 'Project layout' code block lists 'dashboard·board·detail·feed·calendar·cv·network·settings·stats-view·chrome' as if each were one src/ file. `network.tsx` doesn't exist (split into src/companies.tsx and src/contacts.tsx), `settings.tsx` doesn't exist (moved to src/settings/), and neither `stats-view.tsx` nor `chrome.tsx` exist under those names (shell chrome is src/shell.tsx). A newcomer using this as a map to find code will search for files that aren't there.

title: No CHANGELOG despite ~660 merged PRs and real users
why: Multi-user product with an admin/invite model and no way for an invited user to see what changed
detail: No CHANGELOG.md, releases, or in-app 'what's new' surface exists anywhere in the repo (confirmed by filesystem search). With invited users on a live multi-user deployment and PR numbers already past #659, there's no record a non-author user could read to learn what changed between visits. This is a judgment call, not a defect — the product is still author-run — but the invite-only, multi-user framing in CLAUDE.md suggests other people's expectations now matter.

title: docs/superpowers specs are a stale-but-valid archive, not sediment — no action needed
why: Answering the recon question directly: these read as a useful decision record, not clutter
detail: 10 spec files (2026-07-20 through 2026-08-12) each document one shipped feature (digest, timezone, email delivery, fizzy-shell, etc.) and HANDOFF.md itself models good practice by explicitly calling out which of its own citations are stale-but-intentional ('archaeological, by convention', HANDOFF.md:178). The one real currency problem in this set is the screenshot-rig claim (separate finding above); the specs themselves aren't accumulated cruft and don't need pruning.

title: Bus factor is 1, literally: 440/440 commits from a single author
where: git log --format=%an | sort | uniq -c → "440 Ronald Lokers" (whole history)
why: the entire 7-gate verification apparatus is compensating for one person's memory, not proving the codebase is safe for a second contributor
detail: Every commit in the repo's history is by one author. CLAUDE.md (50 lines) plus PRODUCT.md (91 lines) plus 35 test-node specs encode a large amount of implicit product law (stage-colour ΔE2000 rules, pinning semantics, light-only theme, cascade-layer ownership) that a new contributor — human or agent — has to reconstruct from prose before a first PR is safe. There is no architecture doc, no per-surface README, and no CODEOWNERS. If the goal is genuinely a team-scalable public product, the real gap isn't more gates, it's a second person landing an unassisted change and CLAUDE.md/PRODUCT.md surviving contact with someone who didn't write them.

title: The public share page's "never compensation" invariant has zero test enforcement
where: worker/index.ts:1923 (GET /shared/:token); no matching guard in test/api.spec.ts or test-node/
why: the single most privacy-sensitive locked decision in the product ships on prose alone while every other locked decision of comparable weight has a spec file
detail: CLAUDE.md and PRODUCT.md both call out "no compensation" on the public share page as a locked decision, in the same breath as the stage-palette and light-only rules — both of which have hard CI guards (test-node/stage-palette.spec.ts, test-node/locked-decisions.spec.ts). Grepping test/api.spec.ts and test-node/ for "shared"/"compensation" turns up nothing that asserts the aggregate-stats query or its serializer excludes comp fields. A future PR (agent-authored or not) that widens the aggregate to include a salary-adjacent stat would pass every existing gate and ship. This is a five-line assertion to add to test/api.spec.ts, not a redesign.

title: CLAUDE.md's own coverage numbers are already stale against the enforced thresholds
where: CLAUDE.md "Verify before claiming done" (states 31%/25%) vs vitest.config.ts thresholds (statements 43, branches 38, functions 30, lines 43) — floor raised 31→38→43 in commits after e7aadc4 (2026-08-14, CLAUDE.md's last touch)
why: the binding brief has already drifted from the source of truth it's supposed to summarize, on a number that's trivial to keep in sync
detail: The coverage floor has been raised twice since CLAUDE.md last mentioned a number, and nothing re-syncs the two. This is small in isolation but it's evidence for the broader pattern: a 10.8K-word brief that has to be treated as historical rather than authoritative erodes exactly the trust it exists to provide, and there's no test (unlike verification-list.spec.ts, which checks the gate *list* against CI, not the numbers inside it) that would catch this drift automatically.

title: "Icons are line-art SVGs, never emoji" has no CI guard
where: CLAUDE.md "Design: follow the mockup" section; no matching check in test-node/
why: every other similarly-worded locked visual rule (stage hues, light-only theme) has a grep-based spec; this one, equally cheap to enforce, does not
detail: A one-line test-node spec (`grep -rP '\p{Emoji_Presentation}' src/**/*.tsx` excluding test/story files) would close this for the cost of writing it. Currently it's enforceable only by a reviewer noticing, and there is no reviewer but the author.

title: worker/ — including the 2701-line router carrying all authorization logic — has no coverage number at all
where: worker/index.ts (2701 lines); vitest.config.ts coverage.include is "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" only
why: the file that decides who can see what data is the one file the coverage floor structurally cannot see, so a regression that deletes an auth check and still passes 900 tests would not move any measured number
detail: The vitest.config.ts comment is candid and still accurate: @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers loads the worker as a separate pre-bundled module graph, so v8 attributes 0% to it even though the workers project drives it with hundreds of tests — confirmed by re-running `vitest run --project=workers` (366 tests, 62 files, all green). The tests exist; the number doesn't. Fixing this for real means either extracting the authorization/session-gate logic into plain functions importable by the node/component projects (so v8 can instrument them) or waiting on upstream coverage support in vitest-pool-workers — both are real projects, not a config tweak, which is why this has sat as "deliberately unmeasured" rather than fixed.

title: The serial test suite's cost is dominated by per-file workerd startup, not test logic — it will keep growing forever
where: test/ (62 spec files); measured `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism --project=workers`
why: 62 files × ~1.6s startup already costs 98 of 130 seconds; every new spec file is pure serial tax that has nothing to do with what the test asserts
detail: Measured this session: 62 test files, 366 tests, wall time 130.74s, of which the reported breakdown is setup=97.84s vs tests=13.68s — roughly 75% of the run is miniflare/workerd spinning up per file, not test execution. `--no-file-parallelism` is required because parallel runs flake locally (per CLAUDE.md), so the fix isn't "run tests faster" but either root-causing the parallel flake (shared D1/miniflare state race) or restructuring to fewer, larger spec files / a shared worker instance across files. At current growth rate (test/api.spec.ts alone is 943 lines and still growing per recent commits) this gate's wall-clock will keep climbing linearly with file count, independent of how much logic each file actually exercises.

title: The Fizzy-shell redesign shipped, then needed ~30 follow-up fix PRs to reach the bar the process claims to enforce pre-merge
where: git log: #583 "the Fizzy-philosophy shell — every screen redesigned", followed by #585–#622+ (two data bugs, security headers/CSP, design-audit findings ×3, text-resize, modal-escape, contrast, focus-ring, axis/list semantics, landmark, mobile bottom-bar labels, ARIA tablist pattern, tabpanel wiring)
why: the 7-gate loop and "reproduce the mockup faithfully" instruction did not catch a long tail of a11y, contrast, and correctness defects in the redesign that landed before it merged — they were caught after, one PR at a time, over roughly six weeks
detail: CLAUDE.md's "Design: follow the mockup" section asks for a faithful diff against the approved artifact before merge, but the commit log shows the actual practice for large design work is ship-then-audit: #589/#590/#591 are explicitly named "the N findings from the design/shell audit," arriving after #583 merged. This isn't a one-off; it's the visible cost of doing large visual work without a pre-merge accessibility/contrast pass baked into the gate list (axe runs in e2e, but apparently not as a blocking step scoped to a redesign PR). Cheapest fix: run the existing playwright a11y suite against the new screens *before* opening the redesign PR, not treat its findings as separate follow-up work.

title: worker/index.ts is the one router file that never got split, unlike every sibling surface
why: it is still the largest file in the repo, carries the session-auth and admin-role middleware (the two highest-stakes checks in the product), and keeps growing — 6 of the last 10 commits touching it are ordinary feature/fix work, not refactors
detail: CLAUDE.md's editing-conventions section already documents that board.tsx, settings.tsx, and cv.tsx were split out from oversized files as a deliberate pattern, but says nothing about worker/index.ts — the backend file the pattern applies to most, since it's both the biggest file and the one that owns the security-critical middleware boundaries (`:105` security headers, `:240` session gate, `:253` admin gate per the recon digest). Splitting route groups out of it the same way ai.ts/cv.ts/etc. were split would shrink the file a reviewer has to hold in their head to reason about auth.

title: No dependency-update automation for a near-latest-everywhere stack with a 538KB generated, committed type file
where: package.json (typescript ~6.0.2, vite ^8.1.1, react ^19.2.7, storybook ^10.5.2, wrangler ^4.111.0); worker-configuration.d.ts (14,709 lines / 537.9KB, committed); no .github/dependabot.yml or renovate.json in the repo
why: every dependency bump — including the ones that silently invalidate the committed 538KB type file — is a manual, solo decision with no scheduled nudge
detail: The `wrangler types --check` gate is a genuinely good catch (CLAUDE.md documents it caught a stale-branch that passed everything else), but it only fires when someone remembers to bump wrangler/workerd and regenerate. With no bot opening version-bump PRs on a schedule, upgrades happen reactively, batched, and off the back of whatever the author notices — which is a fine posture for a solo hobby project and a real risk for "a polished public product" that wants security patches to land promptly. Adding Dependabot/Renovate for at least security updates is a config file, not a project.

title: Twenty-plus shipped surfaces on one maintainer's capacity — extension and bookmarklet are the least-touched, best freeze candidates
where: src/{board,feed,cv,dashboard,insights,companies,contacts,detail}.tsx, worker/{ai,cv,digest,forwarded-email,goals,push,public-api,calendar}.ts, extension/, src/bookmarklet.ts, worker/admin surfaces — confirmed present via file listing; extension/ last feature-touched at #477/#478, then #659 much later
why: each shipped surface is permanent surface area for the same 7-gate loop and the same one person; the ones least core to the daily pipeline workflow are the cheapest to freeze without losing what makes the product useful
detail: Board/feed/CV/insights/companies are the daily-use core the product brief names as success-critical; ATS scoring, salary/skill-demand research, mock interview, negotiation roleplay, LinkedIn review, the browser extension, and the bookmarklet are all adjacent conveniences layered on top. The browser extension in particular had a multi-PR feature push (#477/#478) and then went quiet for roughly 180 PRs before one more addition (#659) — a pattern consistent with a surface that's shipped but not in active daily iteration, meaning it's accumulating drift risk (browser API changes, manifest v3 policy shifts) with no maintenance cadence. Freezing new feature work on extension/bookmarklet (bug-fix only) would free capacity for the core pipeline surfaces without touching anything the daily-use success metric depends on.

title: feed_items grows forever and the nightly R2 backup serialises the whole database in one Worker
why: An insert-only shared table plus a full in-memory JSON dump is a backup that will silently stop working.
detail: refreshFeed (worker/feed.ts:277) batch-inserts every Adzuna and ATS candidate every six hours with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and nothing anywhere deletes from feed_items — grep for DELETE FROM feed_items returns no hits. runScheduledBackup calls buildFullExport, which does SELECT * over all 27 tables into one JS object and JSON.stringify's it, inside a 128 MB Worker; the failure is swallowed by the independently() catch at worker/index.ts:2645, so the first OOM shows up only as a console line and 14 days later there is no backup. Add a retention sweep (delete feed_items with no feed_item_status row older than ~60 days) and stream the backup table-by-table into R2 rather than building one object.

title: The feed page full-scans and sorts feed_items on every request — the table has no index at all
why: Keyset pagination without a matching index still reads the whole table per page, on a rows-read-billed free tier.
detail: The query orders by COALESCE(feed_items.posted_at, '') DESC, feed_items.id DESC and the only index feed_items ever had was idx_feed_items_status, dropped in migrations/0047_drop_feed_items_status.sql — so the table now carries none. The COALESCE also makes the sort key an expression, so a plain index on posted_at could not serve it even if one existed. Add a partial-null-safe index and rewrite the ordering to match it: CREATE INDEX idx_feed_items_posted ON feed_items(posted_at DESC, id DESC) with ORDER BY posted_at IS NULL, posted_at DESC, id DESC, or an expression index on COALESCE(posted_at,'').

title: Optimistic concurrency from migration 0060 is applied to three of the six full-column PUT forms
why: The CV forms are the same write-every-column shape 0060 was written for and got neither the column nor the precondition.
detail: applications (worker/index.ts:855), companies (:327) and contacts (:414) all read If-Match against updated_at and return 412. PUT /api/work-experience/:id, PUT /api/education/:id (worker/cv.ts:293) and PUT /api/profile (worker/cv.ts:34) write every column from the body with no validator, and their tables never got an updated_at — 0060 added it to contacts and companies only. The client matches: src/cv/sections.tsx:395 and :589 call api.update without an expectedUpdatedAt. Add updated_at to work_experience, education and profile, stamp it on write, and thread the version through the three CV forms.

title: The stale-posting cron is sized for a single user: 15 URLs per run, globally
why: A constant tuned for one account becomes a per-tenant division as soon as a second user exists.
detail: BATCH_SIZE = 15 and the SELECT at worker/posting-check.ts:54 has no user_id predicate, so it takes the 15 least-recently-checked applications across the whole deployment; the cron fires every six hours (shouldRunFeedPull, worker/index.ts:2633), giving 60 checks per day for everyone combined. At the stated ~50 applications per heavy user, three users already means a posting is re-checked roughly every three days, so the board's maybe_stale badge is reporting a state that may be days old. Either scale the batch by active user count or select per user with a per-user cap.

title: worker/index.ts holds three whole subsystems that already have peers as modules
why: The split tracks when a feature was written, not what it is — 45-line modules exist while the router carries 450-line subsystems.
detail: index.ts is 2701 lines and ~75 handlers, and inside it sit the entire server-rendered share page (1732-2185: SHARE_STRINGS, escapeHtml, shareParseSqlDate, sharePageGone and the HTML template), the job-posting URL scraper (1248-1403: decodeEntities, metaContent, findJobPosting), the export/CSV layer (1138-1247) and the cron/backup entry points (2614-2701). Meanwhile worker/goals.ts is 45 lines and worker/documents.ts is 21. Extract share/, import/ and export/ as modules exporting a register*Routes function like every other group; that alone takes ~1000 lines out of the router and gives the share page a place its own tests can address.

title: Defence-in-depth user_id scoping on joins is present on the list routes and missing on /api/agenda and /api/activity
why: Two routes join companies, contacts and applications by id alone while their siblings explicitly refuse to.
detail: I checked all 63 :id-bearing handlers across worker/ mechanically: every one scopes its own row by user_id, and the write paths guard cross-tenant foreign keys through findForeignRef (worker/index.ts:181) — no IDOR found. But /api/applications:483 and /api/contacts:370 carry AND companies.user_id = ... on their joins as an explicit second line of defence from review #445, and /api/agenda (1417, 1428-1432) and /api/activity (1480, 1481) do not — they join LEFT JOIN companies ON companies.id = applications.company_id and JOIN applications a ON a.id = sh.application_id with no owner predicate. Add the same predicates so a stray id can never surface another tenant's name here either.

title: /api/export hands every authenticated user the entire global feed_items table
why: An unbounded SELECT * on a table that only grows, served synchronously to a browser download.
detail: GLOBAL_EXPORT_TABLES (worker/index.ts:1177) makes buildUserExport and GET /api/export/:table fall back to SELECT * FROM feed_items with no user predicate and no LIMIT, on the reasoning that the pool is shared. The rows are public job postings so this is not a tenant leak, but it means one user's export scales with everyone's ingest and with all of history, and feed_items carries the full posting description column added in 0045. Scope the feed export to rows the user actually has a feed_item_status row for, or drop feed_items from the user export entirely and keep it in the admin backup only.

title: No memoization boundary anywhere: the four visible* arrays are rebuilt every render, so App's useMemo never hits
why: A useMemo keyed on an array that is new on every render is a memo that lies.
detail: visibleApps/activeApps/visibleCompanies/visibleContacts (src/app-data.ts:265-276) are bare .filter() calls in the hook body, so their identity changes on every App render; App.tsx:401 then does useMemo(() => visibleApps.filter(...), [visibleApps]) which therefore recomputes unconditionally, and there is no React.memo in the codebase (grep for memo( across src returns nothing). Because the toast queue lives in the same component (src/App.tsx:169), every toast push and every 3s/6s expiry re-renders the whole tree, including board.tsx:1019's applications x history aggregation pass. Wrap the four filters in useMemo and memo the tab bodies, or move the toast queue below the tabs.

title: npm run lint does not fail on warnings, so the zero-warning gate CLAUDE.md relies on is not enforced
why: CI runs a command that exits 0 with warnings present, on a rule the working guide singles out by name.
detail: The script is bare `oxlint` and .github/workflows/ci.yml:23 runs it as-is. I proved the gap: a probe component with useEffect(() => setN(n+1), []) written into src/ produced `warning react-hooks(exhaustive-deps)` and exit code 0 under the project config, and exit 1 only when --deny was passed. The repo is clean today (full oxlint run: 0 findings, exit 0), so this is a hole not yet fallen into. Change the script to `oxlint --max-warnings=0`, or promote react/exhaustive-deps to error in .oxlintrc.json.

title: The share page carries a second, hand-written translation table outside the locale-parity gate
why: Strict en/nl parity is enforced for src/locales and silently not enforced for the one page strangers see.
detail: SHARE_STRINGS is an inline en/nl object literal in the router, selected by shareLocale (worker/index.ts:1852) from Accept-Language and the owner's locale. test-node/locale-parity.spec.ts only walks src/locales/en.json and nl.json, so a key added to one half of SHARE_STRINGS and not the other ships, and the planned third locale means adding a language in two unrelated places. Move the share strings into src/locales under a `share.` namespace the worker imports (it already type-imports from src/types.ts at worker/index.ts:26), or extend the parity spec to cover this object.

title: setStatus closes over the whole applications array, so its identity changes on every data change
why: A callback threaded to every tab is invalidated by data it only needs for a rollback snapshot.
detail: The dep array is [applications, reload, refreshStats, notify, navigate, t]; `applications` is only read to capture `prev` for the failure rollback and to look up prevStatus. Both can come from the functional setState form (setApplications(cur => { ... })) or a ref, which drops `applications` from the deps and makes setStatus stable for the life of the hook. Same shape as the visible* arrays above — together they are why nothing downstream can usefully be memoized.

title: Push delivery does one UPDATE round-trip per notification instead of one batch
why: An N+1 write inside a cron that already knows the full id set up front.
detail: The Promise.all maps each due row to sendPushToUser followed by its own `UPDATE notifications SET pushed_at = ... WHERE id = ?`. The email leg two lines below already groups by user before doing its work, and refreshFeed and checkStalePostings both use env.DB.batch for exactly this. Collect the successfully-pushed ids and issue one env.DB.batch (guarded for the empty case, as worker/posting-check.ts:89 already is).

title: FeedSettings — 340 lines of settings UI — lives in src/feed.tsx and is statically imported by the settings page
why: A settings panel outside src/settings/ that welds two lazy route chunks together.
detail: src/settings/index.tsx:20 does `import { FeedSettings } from "../feed"`, so opening Settings pulls the feed chunk (feed-Bv14BsZh.js, 16.58 kB) even though the user never opened the Feed tab, and vice versa. The file's own comment at src/settings/index.tsx:2 acknowledges the coupling as a circular-import workaround. Move FeedSettings into src/settings/feed-settings.tsx; the feed tab does not import it, so nothing else has to change.

title: The critical-path bundle is ~172 kB gzipped and manualChunks only splits react and i18n
why: Mobile first paint is a locked target and the entry chunk carries the dashboard, insights, format and the whole English locale.
detail: Measured from npm run build: react 222.88 kB (71.44 gz) + entry index-WgY5NST5.js 198.59 kB (59.97 gz) + i18n 62.47 kB (20.42 gz) + one render-blocking index.css at 116.05 kB (19.74 gz). The heavy leaves are correctly lazy (pdf 406 kB, html2canvas 199 kB, jspdf 151 kB all sit behind the dynamic imports in src/cv.tsx:206 and src/format.ts:372), and nl.json is its own 41 kB chunk — but en.json is not, so ~40 kB of locale JSON is in the entry, and dashboard.tsx (833 lines) and insights.tsx (544) are too because only board/feed/detail/settings/cv/admin/companies/contacts are lazy. Lazy-load en the way nl already is (src/i18n.ts:43) and split insights out of the entry.

title: detail.tsx is long, not complex — the only real front-end hotspot is board.tsx
why: Answering the brief: two of the three named files are size, one is cost.
detail: detail.tsx is a single 890-line JSX component with 14 useState, zero useMemo/useCallback and no loops over collections — flat markup with inline handlers, cheap to render and safe to leave alone beyond extracting the follow-up and outcome panels. feed.tsx is three unrelated components in one file (FeedSettings 29-367, FeedTab 368-1053, FeedCard 1056-1228). board.tsx:1019 is the genuine hotspot: an applications x status_history x interactions aggregation building six Maps, whose stated purpose (keeping the pass off every search keystroke) holds, but which re-runs on every parent render because its `applications` prop is a fresh array — see the memoization finding.

title: Dependencies are clean; the one oddity is a major-behind pin on the web-push crypto library
why: Everything else is within one minor and audit is empty, so this is the only dependency worth a decision.
detail: npm audit --omit=dev reports 0 vulnerabilities. npm outdated shows every runtime dep within one minor except @block65/webcrypto-web-push, pinned ^1.0.2 against a 2.0.0 published 2026-09-03 — a small single-purpose MIT package on the VAPID signing path, actively maintained rather than abandoned. Dev tooling is a major behind in three places (vitest/coverage-v8 4→5, jsdom 25→30, typescript 6→7) which is fine to defer. Read the 2.0.0 changelog and either bump or record why not; a security fix in that library is not something the app would otherwise notice.

title: Insights tab (and its Calendar/Activity import) ships in the main bundle, not lazy like every other tab
why: The literal string "insights.headlineNumbers" appears once in dist/client/assets/index-WgY5NST5.js (198.59kB raw / 59.97kB gzip) and zero times in any other chunk — Insights' 544 lines are compiled into the main entry, not a lazy chunk.
detail: App.tsx lazy()-loads seven tab bodies (settings, feed, companies, contacts, cv, detail, board, admin) behind Suspense, but `import { InsightsTab } from "./insights"` at line 31 is a static import, same as Dashboard. Dashboard being eager is deliberate (default landing view, per the comment at App.tsx:33-36); nothing explains why Insights — a non-default tab — gets the same treatment. Insights also statically imports calendar.tsx (183 lines, ActivityTab+CalendarTab), which rides along into the main chunk too since nothing else imports it. Fix: `const InsightsTab = lazy(() => import("./insights").then(m => ({ default: m.InsightsTab })))`, matching the existing pattern one line above it.

title: jsPDF and html2canvas are correctly deferred — confirmed, not a finding to fix
why: pdf-DR8Ditpa.js is 406.60kB raw / 131.76kB gzip and only network-requested on the dynamic `await import("./pdf")` call sites, not on initial load or on visiting the CV tab.
detail: Both call sites (generateCvPdf/generateCvPdfTwoColumn in cv.tsx:206, generateInterviewCheatSheet in detail.tsx:226) are dynamic imports fired only when the user actually exports something — jsPDF's real dependency html2canvas (199.56kB/46.78kB gzip) is its own separate chunk for the same reason. Recorded here because the task asked to verify it explicitly; no action needed. Keep it this way if pdf.ts ever grows a new caller — a static top-level import anywhere in the cv/ or detail module tree would pull 606kB raw back into a route chunk.

title: The weekly-goal row is fetched twice, independently, on every Overview visit
why: Four separate call sites for the same api.goals() row; on a captured cold load of '/' the live app fired /api/goals 4 times (2 distinct call sites x React 18/19 StrictMode's dev-only double-invoke) instead of once.
detail: App.tsx's onboarding-probe effect (line 227-245) and DashboardTab's own effect (dashboard.tsx:71-75) both call api.goals() independently whenever the Overview tab mounts, with no cache or shared fetch between them — each is a full round trip through the session-auth middleware to a D1 read. Because DashboardTab unmounts/remounts on every tab switch (App.tsx conditionally renders it), this refetch repeats every time the user returns to Overview. Fix: lift the goal fetch into useAppData alongside the other five resources, or thread the value App.tsx already asks for down as a prop instead of having Dashboard ask again.

title: reload() refetches all 5 top-level resources (>=8 D1 statements) on every mutation, even single-field edits
where: src/app-data.ts:102-127, src/App.tsx:672,723,738,765,795,816, worker/index.ts:481 (2 statements), worker/index.ts:1514 (3 statements)
why: onChanged={reload} is wired to 6 separate call sites in App.tsx; each firing re-issues applications (2 D1 statements: worker/index.ts:481-508), companies, contacts, roleTypes, and stats (3 statements: worker/index.ts:1514-1552) — at least 8 D1 statements for one save.
detail: reload() (app-data.ts:102) is the app's only full-refresh path, and it is what onChanged fires after saving a company edit, adding a contact, editing an application field, changing role types, or anything the Feed/Companies/Contacts/Settings tabs do. The one place that already avoids this is the board's drag-and-drop status change, which calls the narrower refreshStats() (app-data.ts:133-138, /api/stats only) after an optimistic local update — proving the narrower path is already a known, working pattern. On the free tier, D1 row reads are the metered resource, so a company-name edit costing the same 8 statements as a cold load is the kind of amplification worth fixing before usage grows past one user. Fix: give tag/contact/company mutations their own targeted setters (mirroring setStatus's optimistic-update + refreshStats shape) instead of routing every one of them through reload().

title: BoardCard is unmemoized and receives fresh closures every render — full board re-renders on every board search keystroke
where: src/board.tsx:63-89 (BoardCard), src/board.tsx:432-441 (cardProps), src/board.tsx:658-675 (cards.map), src/board.tsx:1168 (setQuery on keystroke)
why: cardProps(a) at board.tsx:432 is a plain function called fresh per card per render (board.tsx:673), constructing 5 new callback closures each time, and BoardCard itself has no React.memo wrapper — so any state change in the board (a keystroke in the search box at board.tsx:1163-1168) re-renders every visible card, not just the ones whose data changed.
detail: No virtualization is a locked product decision for ~50 applications, and that's fine — the issue isn't rendering all the cards, it's redoing the render (translation lookups via t(), formatDate, totalComp, className template strings) for cards whose data hasn't changed, on every keystroke of an unrelated search box. Fix: wrap BoardCard in React.memo and stabilize the 7 handler props with useCallback (or a per-application memoized handler map) — cheap and low-risk since BoardCard's own render has no side effects to worry about.

title: Onboarding probes (profile/feed-config/goals) fetch on every load until the user explicitly clicks Dismiss, even after the checklist naturally stops appearing
why: The effect's only gate is `if (onboardingDismissed) return` (App.tsx:228); onboardingComplete becoming true only hides the checklist UI (showOnboarding, line 431-435), it never sets the dismissed flag — so 3 extra requests (api.profile, api.feedConfig, api.goals) fire on every single load for any user who completed onboarding without ever pressing the explicit dismiss button.
detail: For an established daily user this is 3 always-on requests riding along on top of the 5-endpoint reload() and the goals double-fetch (finding above) on every app open, forever, unless they happened to click Dismiss at some point. Cheap individually but permanent and silent. Fix: also persist the dismissed flag once onboardingComplete is observed true, the same way an explicit dismiss does today.

title: Main chunk (still 198.59kB raw / 59.97kB gzip) is the largest single JS asset users load before interacting
why: Measured via `npm run build`: main entry 198.59kB/59.97kB gzip, react vendor chunk 222.88kB/71.44kB gzip, i18n vendor chunk 62.47kB/20.42kB gzip (English only; nl-B2_Hu7JW.js 41.67kB/15.63kB gzip loads separately for Dutch users) — total initial JS ~484.5kB raw / ~152.2kB gzip, plus CSS 116.05kB/19.74kB gzip and 2 preloaded font subsets (~52kB combined, woff2).
detail: vite.config.ts already manually splits React and i18next out of the main chunk (comment at line 9 cites #346); the remaining main-chunk weight is largely App.tsx's own shell code plus the two eagerly-bundled tabs from the first finding above. Once Insights/Calendar move to lazy(), re-measure — the main chunk should drop noticeably since Insights alone is 544 lines with its own charts/skill-gap logic.

title: Dev-server runtime timing (DCL/LCP/long-tasks) captured this session is not representative of production and should be re-measured against a built app
why: Playwright against the live dev server recorded 125-127 separate script requests per route (unbundled ES modules, vite's dev transform) and DomContentLoaded varying 3.1s-8.7s across two runs of the same route — both artifacts of unbundled dev serving and on-demand transform latency, not the shipped app.
detail: Chrome's LargestContentfulPaint entry also never fired in either capture (even after forcing a visibility change, the standard trick to flush it) — worth rechecking against `wrangler dev` serving the production build, where module count drops to roughly 8-10 static assets (matching finding above) and LCP should resolve normally. What is trustworthy from this session: the API waterfall (identical endpoint set, same request count pattern, fired in parallel not chained) and the production bundle sizes from `npm run build`, both reported as separate confirmed findings. Recommend re-running this exact measurement against `npm run build` + `wrangler dev` before trusting any absolute load-time number for Zenith.

title: Cold load fires 12 distinct API endpoints in parallel (not chained) totalling ~38.4kB of JSON
why: Captured content-length sum across /api/applications (19,435B), /api/stats (9,315B), /api/contacts (3,183B), /api/companies (2,935B), /api/feed/config (1,023B), /api/profile (634B), /api/auth/get-session (673B), /api/notifications (544B), /api/role-types (435B), /api/goals (104B), /api/preferences (86B), /api/ai/credentials (33B) = 38,400 bytes uncompressed.
detail: This is the good news half of the waterfall question: useAppData's reload() uses Promise.all (app-data.ts:104-112, 5 requests), the timezone probe (150-159) and the onboarding probes (App.tsx:229-241) are independent effects that don't block each other or reload(), so nothing here is a serial chain — every request starts at once. /api/applications dominates the payload at 19.4kB for 18 seeded rows; at the locked ~50-application ceiling this scales linearly to roughly 50-55kB, still small, but it is the one response worth watching if per-application payload (tags, joined names) grows further.

title: Diagnostic layer ignores the origin data it already captures
where: src/insights.tsx:111-277 (KPI band + funnel, no origin dimension); worker/feed.ts:608 (source column written); src/detail.tsx:406 (referred_by_contact_id shown, never aggregated)
why: The product's second positioning claim and its stated secondary success metric are both 'diagnose why the search went the way it did' by channel, but the channel data is captured and thrown away.
detail: Every application already carries `source` (`feed:adzuna`, `feed:greenhouse:...`, `extension`, manual) and `referred_by_contact_id`, and companies carry `is_agency` — but Insights (src/insights.tsx) never groups response rate, funnel conversion, or ghost rate by any of them. A user cannot answer 'is the feed worth the 6-hourly cron' or 'are referrals actually converting better than cold applies' even though the answer is sitting in the DB. This is the single highest-leverage gap: it turns on data already stored, needs no new schema, and it's exactly the 'diagnose' half of the product promise that a plain list-of-applications tracker (the stated non-differentiator) cannot do either — right now Zenith doesn't do it either.

title: Browser extension is fully built but invisible inside the app
where: extension/README.md:14 (instructs user to create a key under 'Settings → Integrations'); src/settings/api.tsx:130-176 (that section exists but never mentions the extension); src/components/OnboardingChecklist.tsx:57-75 (checklist has no extension step)
why: The one-click save + autofill browser extension is a real, working differentiator against Huntr/Simplify/Teal (all of whom lead their marketing with exactly this), and a first-time user who 'has never met the author' (per PRODUCT.md) has no way to discover it exists.
detail: The extension (extension/) does one-click job save with structured-data scraping and ATS form autofill — genuinely comparable to what competitors ship as their headline feature. But it is not linked from Settings, not in the onboarding checklist, not mentioned in-app anywhere; its own README assumes an in-app 'Settings → Integrations' surface that doesn't exist under that name. Fix is a Settings card (mirroring the existing bookmarklet-section.tsx pattern) with the install steps and a link to the API key generator already on that page, plus a sixth onboarding-checklist item.

title: No duplicate-application detection on any create path
where: worker/index.ts:725-745 (POST /api/applications); worker/feed.ts:608-637 (feed add-to-pipeline); extension/README.md:27 (extension POSTs the same endpoint)
why: A silently duplicated application (same URL re-added from a refreshed feed, or the extension used twice on the same posting) inflates every funnel/response-rate/ghost-rate number the product exists to produce.
detail: None of the three creation paths (manual add, feed 'add to pipeline', extension save) check for an existing application with the same URL or the same company+title for the user before inserting. At ~50 tracked applications with a feed re-pulling every 6 hours and a same posting sometimes appearing under slightly different titles, this is a realistic, silent way to corrupt the exact stats (conversion funnel, response rate) that are the product's stated spine. Fix: a pre-insert check by normalized URL (and a soft company+title match) that returns a 409 with the existing application id, surfaced in the UI as 'You already have this one — open it?' rather than a hard block.

title: Interview prep checklist is invisible to the 'what do I do now' screen
where: src/dashboard.tsx:366-404 (NextUpPanel reads only next_action/next_action_at); src/detail.tsx:223 (interview_prep_items fetched only inside the detail page's Prep tab)
why: Two features that both answer 'what do I do before this interview' don't talk to each other, so the Today screen — the app's whole reason for existing per PRODUCT.md ('know the next action within seconds') — can go blank while an interview two days out still has four unchecked prep items.
detail: dashboard.tsx's Next Up panel ranks and surfaces rows purely off `next_action`/`next_action_at`, which the user must type by hand (the seed data shows this: 'PREPARE FOR THE ONSITE' as manually-set next_action text). It never reads `interview_prep_items`, so an application with real, tracked, unchecked prep tasks and no manually-typed next_action is silent on Today. Cheapest fix: when an application is in the interview stage with open prep items and no next_action set, synthesize a 'finish interview prep (n left)' row from the prep-item count rather than requiring the user to duplicate that state as free text.

title: Board stacks two redundant 'everything is folded' banners at once
why: When a user folds every live stage while a closed rail is still expanded, the board shows two overlapping banners with two different undo links, which reads as broken chrome on the primary pipeline screen.
detail: The condition at line 499 (`CLOSED_RAILS.some((r) => !shownFolded.has(r))`, guarded by `!closedGrouped && !isNarrow && !pinnedOnly`) and the condition at line 514 (`PIPELINE.every((r) => shownFolded.has(r))`) are independent booleans that can both be true simultaneously — confirmed live during recon ('Closed applications are showing. Fold them away' stacked directly above 'Every live stage is folded — only closed applications are showing. Back to live'). Fix: make the all-folded banner supersede the closed-open banner (it's the superset condition) by adding `&& !PIPELINE.every((r) => shownFolded.has(r))` to the first guard.

title: Board-card company chip truncates mid-word with no ellipsis
why: The board is the app's primary daily-scan surface, and every unfolded-column card reads a hard-clipped company name ('SOLACE SYSTEMS · DIE', 'BRIGHTPATH TALENT P') with no visual cue that it's cut off, which undercuts the one thing a kanban view is supposed to do: scan fast.
detail: CSS declares `text-overflow: ellipsis` on `.bstrip > span` (App.css:5555) but `.bstrip` also sets `letter-spacing: var(--track-eyebrow)` (App.css:5541) — verified live in board-desktop.png, every company chip clips a hard character boundary with zero '…' rendered, a known Chromium/WebKit interaction where letter-spacing suppresses the ellipsis glyph. The `title` attribute (board.tsx:120) is the only fallback, and it's invisible on mobile (no hover). Fix: drop letter-spacing on `.bco` specifically (it doesn't need the eyebrow tracking the date cell does), or widen the column's min-width for that cell.

title: CV builder versions never link to the application that used them
where: src/detail.tsx:798-799 (generic Documents component, no cv_version reference); no reference to cv_versions anywhere in src/detail.tsx
why: The CV builder's own versioning (a confirmed capability per PRODUCT.md) has no path back to the applications it was used on, so the product can never answer 'does my tailored resume actually get more responses than my generic one' — a question every one of the ~50 applications could answer.
detail: Application detail's Documents tab is a bare per-application file upload (`<Documents applicationId={a.id} />`), entirely separate from `cv_versions`. There is no field recording which CV version (if any) accompanied a given application, so response-rate-by-résumé-version is structurally impossible even though both halves of the data (the version, the outcome) already exist. Smallest version: add an optional `cv_version_id` to `applications`, a picker in the detail page's document section defaulting to 'none', and one more Insights breakdown alongside the existing outcome/funnel cards.

title: README.md contradicts the locked light-only decision and describes a stale file layout
where: README.md:42 ('Three themes (Automatic / Light / Dark)'); README.md:90 (project layout lists network·stats-view·chrome as files)
why: README.md is the first thing a stranger reads (PRODUCT.md: 'a first-time user who has never met the author'), and it currently promises a theme switcher that was deliberately removed and describes source files that no longer exist, undermining the 'personal-tool craft at product polish' positioning claim on the very first impression.
detail: Line 42 claims 'Three themes (Automatic / Light / Dark)' — CLAUDE.md and PRODUCT.md are explicit that Light is the only theme and `test-node/locked-decisions.spec.ts` fails if dark/auto ever reappear, so this line is not aspirational drift, it's actively wrong today. Line 90's project layout still names `network` (split into companies.tsx/contacts.tsx per CLAUDE.md's own editing-conventions note), `stats-view` and a bare `chrome` file, none of which match current src/. Fix is a five-minute edit: drop the themes line, regenerate the layout list from src/.

title: Feed triage has no signal for 'I already looked at this company'
where: src/feed.tsx (swipe/triage list, no per-company history indicator); worker/feed.ts (feed_company_blocklist exists only as an opt-out list, not a soft signal)
why: A heavy user running 6-hourly feed pulls across Adzuna/Greenhouse/Ashby will see the same employer resurface under a new req multiple times a month, and the triage card gives no hint that this company already has a live or closed application — the blocklist is a hard opt-out, not the softer 'you've been here before' cue.
detail: feed_company_blocklist lets a user fully exclude a company from the feed, but there's nothing between 'never show me this company again' and 'show it exactly like a company I've never seen.' A one-line badge on the triage card ('2 open applications here' / 'you applied here in March, rejected') would let the user swipe faster and more confidently on a repeat employer instead of re-researching it.
