Not verified against every code path in feed.tsx given the file's size (1228 lines); confidence is likely, not confirmed, pending a closer read of the card-rendering function.

title: Recruiter/hiring-manager PII in `contacts` has no lawful-basis story, no retention limit, and no notice — only a manual delete
why: The operator is a GDPR controller for data about recruiters/hiring managers who never consented and have no way to know it exists
detail: Contacts hold third-party name, email, phone, LinkedIn and free-text notes entered by the user, with no data-subject notice, no automatic expiry, and no mechanism for the contact to find out about or request deletion of their own data (only the account owner can delete a row, and only if they think to). Legitimate interest is the plausible lawful basis (a job-seeker's own records of people who contacted them professionally), but nothing in the product states that, bounds how long it's kept, or explains it anywhere a data subject could find it. Minimal responsible fix for a personal tool: one line in a privacy notice naming the basis and a stated retention ceiling (e.g. tied to the parent application's archive), not a consent flow.

title: No privacy notice anywhere in the product for GDPR Art. 13/14 disclosure
where: no privacy policy found in repo (checked README.md, SELF_HOSTING.md, src/locales/en.json, src/settings/*)
why: A controller processing personal data (users' own PII plus third-party contact PII) must tell data subjects what is processed and why; nothing does
detail: There is no privacy-policy page, no link to one, and no in-app notice describing what is collected, the lawful basis, retention, or who to contact — required for both the account holder (Art. 13) and, separately, for the recruiters/hiring managers whose data is entered by someone else (Art. 14). The AI-key settings copy (`src/locales/en.json:707`) is the one place this is done well and can be the template: state plainly, in one place, what's collected and why.

title: Daily full-database R2 backups retain every user's data 14 days with no link to account deletion or export
where: worker/index.ts:2617 (runScheduledBackup), worker/index.ts:1179 (buildFullExport — all users, all EXPORT_TABLES)
why: A deleted account's data (and third-party contact PII) still exists in plaintext JSON in R2 for up to 14 days after deletion, undocumented anywhere
detail: `runScheduledBackup` dumps every user's rows (via `buildFullExport`, unscoped) into one JSON object per day in `DOCS`, pruned to the last 14 (`BACKUP_RETENTION`). This is reasonable disaster-recovery practice, but it means `DELETE /api/account` does not actually erase a user within 14 days, and nothing tells the user that. A one-line addition to a privacy notice ("deleted data may persist in backups for up to 14 days") closes the gap cheaply; no code change is required.

title: Account deletion and per-account wipe are actually thorough — D1 rows, R2 documents, and push subscriptions are all covered
why: Verified end to end: this is the one area of the product doing right-to-erasure correctly and should be the reference for the rest
detail: `wipeUserData` deletes the R2 objects behind every `documents` row first (so a bucket failure leaves the DB rows intact for a retry, rather than orphaning files), then deletes every table in `USER_TABLES` — which explicitly includes `push_subscriptions`, `ai_credentials`, `cv_versions`, `outreach_templates` and `user_goals` after a prior gap (per its own comment) left those undeleted. `DELETE /api/account` calls this then deletes the user row itself. The only residual is the 14-day backup window (separate finding) — nothing else needs fixing here.

title: `/api/export` omits the actual R2 file bytes for CVs/cover letters — portability is metadata-only for documents
where: worker/index.ts:1140 (EXPORT_TABLES includes "documents"), worker/index.ts:1206 (GET /api/export), migrations/0004_documents.sql:2 (documents row = key/filename/size, not content)
why: GDPR Art. 20 portability implies the data itself, not just a pointer to a file the export doesn't include
detail: The `documents` table only stores R2 keys/filenames/sizes, never file content, so a full JSON export names every CV/cover-letter file without including it — a user exporting their data to leave the product does not get their actual documents. Fix is bounded: either bundle the R2 objects into a zip alongside the JSON, or add a short-lived signed download link per document in the export payload.

title: Better Auth `admin()` plugin is enabled with defaults, which includes account impersonation, with no audit surfaced to the impersonated user
why: Any admin can silently assume any user's session and read their CV, compensation figures and private interviewer notes; the product is invite-only multi-user, not single-tenant
detail: The schema (`session.impersonatedBy`) and the plugin configuration (`admin()` called with no options) confirm impersonation is available to any admin-role user, and nothing in the codebase restricts or logs it back to the affected user. PRODUCT.md notes admins and users are "the same people" today, which makes this theoretical now, but the product's own ambition is a wider invite-only user base — the capability should either be disabled (`admin({ impersonationSessionDuration: 0 })`-style config or a stricter role check) or surfaced to the user (a visible "an admin accessed your account" notice) before that happens.

title: Auth `session` rows (with IP address + user agent) and `rateLimit` rows are never purged after expiry
where: migrations/0023_better_auth.sql:20 (session.ipAddress/userAgent, no expiry job), migrations/0046_rate_limit.sql:9 (rateLimit, no pruning found)
why: IP address is personal data under GDPR; Better Auth checks `expiresAt` on read but nothing in this codebase deletes the row afterward, so it accumulates forever
detail: Grepping worker/ found no cron or route that deletes expired `session` or stale `rateLimit` rows — Better Auth treats an expired session as invalid but doesn't clean up the table itself unless the host app schedules it. Over the life of an account this silently accumulates IP/user-agent history with no minimization argument for keeping it past expiry. Minimal fix: add a daily cron step (there is already a daily 03:00 backup cron to piggyback on) that runs `DELETE FROM session WHERE expiresAt < datetime('now')` and prunes `rateLimit` rows older than its window.

title: No LICENSE file despite a public GitHub repo and a SELF_HOSTING.md that invites cloning and deployment
where: repo root (no LICENSE/LICENSE.md found), package.json (no "license" field), SELF_HOSTING.md:1
why: Without a license, default copyright applies and nobody actually has permission to self-host the code the docs invite them to clone
detail: `SELF_HOSTING.md` walks a reader through `git clone https://github.com/ronaldlokers/Zenith.git` and standing up their own copy, but there is no LICENSE file and no `license` field in package.json — under default copyright law the repository being public and readable doesn't grant reuse rights, so the self-hosting instructions are legally unbacked. This is a one-file fix once the author decides terms (even a restrictive "source-available, no commercial use" license is fine); the risk is only in the current silence, not in any particular choice.

title: Public `/shared/:token` and `/calendar/:token` are well-scoped, but the ICS endpoint has no explicit no-index signal to match the HTML page's
where: worker/index.ts:2068 (meta robots noindex on the HTML share page), worker/calendar.ts:260 (ICS response headers — no X-Robots-Tag)
why: The share page explicitly opts out of indexing; the calendar feed, which also carries a per-user unguessable token in its URL, doesn't carry the equivalent header
detail: The share page correctly sends `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` (also present on the revoked-link page). The ICS feed is `text/calendar`, which crawlers essentially never index, so real-world risk is negligible, but for parity and defense-in-depth an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header on the `/calendar/:token` response costs one line and removes the asymmetry. Content itself is already scoped well: interview notes are deliberately excluded (see the comment at worker/calendar.ts:~218 citing #450) and events are marked CLASS:PRIVATE/TRANSPARENT.

title: The generic error handler logs raw error objects, which could echo request-derived text into Cloudflare's observability logs
where: worker/index.ts:2568 (app.onError -> console.error(err)), worker/email/index.ts:32 (console.error("email send failed", err))
why: Observability is enabled in wrangler.jsonc, so anything written to console.error is retained in Cloudflare's log platform outside the app's own data boundary
detail: Only two console.error call sites were found in worker/, and neither directly logs an email address, token or CV body in the code as written — but both log the full `Error` object, whose `.message` can carry provider-response text (e.g. from Resend) or D1 constraint detail that may include user-supplied content depending on what threw. Not a confirmed leak, but worth a pass to confirm no code path's thrown message ever embeds an email/name/notes value before this is treated as safe. Low cost to check, since the call sites are few.

title: AI settings copy discloses CV+JD sent to Anthropic, but not what mock-interview/negotiation roleplay sends
where: src/locales/en.json:707 (aiKeyHint, names CV + job description only), worker/ai.ts:502 (mock-interview), worker/ai.ts:538 (negotiation)
why: The one disclosure string in the product doesn't cover two of its four AI features, both of which can carry salary figures the user types into the roleplay
detail: `tailor-cv` matches its disclosure exactly (CV summary + work-experience descriptions + pasted JD, per worker/ai.ts:421-448). `mock-interview` and `negotiation` send whatever free-text the user types across up to 40 turns (worker/ai.ts:515-524, 549-555) — for negotiation specifically, that's likely to include real compensation numbers — under the same BYO key, but the settings page's one disclosure line doesn't mention this. Low severity because the user is typing the content themselves in the moment (self-evident what's being sent) and it's already gated behind their own key, but the per-feature hint strings (`src/locales/en.json:400,409`) could each state "sent to Anthropic" explicitly rather than only "using your own Anthropic key", which reads as a billing note more than a data-flow one.

title: Optimistic status revert can wipe a concurrent, successful status change
why: A user who moves two cards in quick succession can have a later, successful move silently reverted just because an earlier, unrelated move's API call failed.
detail: setStatus captures `prev = applications` from the render it was created in, then on API failure does `setApplications(prev)` (src/app-data.ts:246) — a full-array replace, not a per-row revert. If a second setStatus call fires before React re-renders (same stale `applications` closure, e.g. two rapid drags), both optimistic updates land via the functional setApplications form, but if the FIRST call's request then fails, its catch block stomps the entire array back to the pre-both-updates snapshot, discarding the second call's already-successful change with no error shown for it. Fix: revert only the one row (e.g. `setApplications(apps => apps.map(a => a.id===id ? {...a, status: prevStatus, updated_at: prevUpdatedAt} : a))`) instead of restoring the whole array. Untested: no spec references `setStatus` directly.

title: Two "way back" banners stack when the Closed-applications action fires
why: Using the board's own "Closed applications" shortcut/menu item shows two overlapping undo banners instead of one, reading as broken rather than helpful.
detail: The `closedOpen` banner renders whenever any closed rail is unfolded and the group isn't collapsed (`CLOSED_RAILS.some(r => !shownFolded.has(r))`, line 502), and the `allLiveFolded` banner renders whenever every pipeline rail is folded (`PIPELINE.every(r => shownFolded.has(r))`, line 515). The board's own "Closed applications" action (line 887-899, triggered by the menu, the 'A' key, and the Insights link) does exactly both at once: `applyFold(new Set(PIPELINE), before)` folds every live stage AND replaces the fold set so no closed rail is folded, satisfying both conditions simultaneously — reproduced live in the recon screenshot pass. Fix: make the two conditions mutually exclusive, or merge them into one message when both are true.

title: fit_score range check exists only on PATCH, not on POST/PUT applications
why: Creating or fully editing an application can store a fit_score outside 1-5 (e.g. -50 or 999), silently corrupting the board's fit-sort order and the feed's match-band thresholds, which assume the range PATCH alone enforces.
detail: `app.patch("/api/applications/:id")` validates `Number.isInteger(fit) && fit >= 1 && fit <= 5` (worker/index.ts:1034) before writing fit_score, but `app.post("/api/applications")` and `app.put("/api/applications/:id")` both pass `body.fit_score` straight into `applicationValues()` (line 159) with no such check, and there is no DB CHECK constraint on the column either (only `ALTER TABLE applications ADD COLUMN fit_score INTEGER` in migrations/0018). `sortCards`'s `fit` sort (src/format.ts:301-302) and `matchBand` (src/format.ts:93-96) both trust the stored value's range. Fix: move the PATCH validation into `applicationValues`/a shared validator so POST and PUT can't bypass it.

title: Compensation fields (salary, bonus, equity) have no range validation anywhere
why: A negative salary or an absurd bonus percentage is accepted and then shown back to the user in the offer comparison, PDF export, and the negotiation-draft prose it feeds, undermining the exact numbers a real salary conversation relies on.
detail: salary_min/salary_max (migrations/0009), signing_bonus/bonus_target_pct/equity_value (migrations/0011) have no CHECK constraint, and none of POST/PUT/PATCH validate them — `applicationValues()` (worker/index.ts:140-173) binds whatever the client sends. `totalComp()`/`totalCompBreakdown()` (src/format.ts:359-364, 448-459) compute `bonus = base * bonus_target_pct / 100` unconditionally, so e.g. `bonus_target_pct: 500` produces a 5x-base 'bonus' baked into the PDF (`downloadOfferComparisonPdf`) and the negotiation draft (`buildNegotiationDraft`) with no sanity bound. Fix: add reasonable bounds (salary_min>=0, salary_max>=salary_min, 0<=bonus_target_pct<=~200) either as app-level validation or DB CHECK constraints.

title: Board company chip clips mid-word with no visible ellipsis on cramped columns
why: With several columns unfolded, company names read as broken fragments ("SOLACE SYSTEMS · DIE", "BRIGHTPATH TALENT P") instead of a legible truncation, on the field the app's own code comment calls the second thing a job hunter navigates by.
detail: `.bstrip > span` (src/App.css:5548-5556) sets `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, which should apply to `.bco` (a direct child span, src/board.tsx:119-125). The live board-desktop screenshot shows the text hard-clipped with no '…' glyph at all. `.bstrip` also carries `letter-spacing: var(--track-eyebrow)` (line 5541) on the same uppercase mono strip — a known browser interaction where trailing letter-spacing after the last visible character pushes the ellipsis glyph itself past the overflow-hidden edge, so it never paints. The `title` attribute (board.tsx:121) is the only fallback, which needs a hover/long-press. Fix: verify by removing letter-spacing on this span in isolation; if confirmed, reset `letter-spacing: normal` on the ellipsis-bearing span or pad the box to compensate.

title: Document upload size cap trusts the client-declared Content-Length, never measures actual bytes
why: A client that understates its own Content-Length header can push an arbitrarily large file past the documented 10 MB cap into R2, and the stored `size` column then permanently misreports what's actually stored.
detail: `const size = Number(c.req.header("Content-Length") ?? 0)` (line 2203) is the sole input to both the `size > MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` gate (line 2205) and the `size` value written to the `documents` row (line 2239, 2239) — the raw body stream (`c.req.raw.body`, line 2229) is piped straight to `c.env.DOCS.put()` without counting bytes. The app's own client always sets Content-Length correctly (fetch with a File body, src/api.ts:375-397), so this only matters against a misbehaving/hostile authenticated client, but the free-tier R2 budget CLAUDE.md calls out as a real constraint has no enforcement against it. Fix: wrap the body in a counting stream (or buffer it) and re-check the real length before/while writing to R2.

title: Interaction happened_at accepts any string, no date validation
why: A garbled or non-date happened_at silently breaks sort order and the momentum/response-time stats that read it, with no error surfaced anywhere in the chain.
detail: Both `POST /api/applications/:id/interactions` and `POST /api/contacts/:id/interactions` bind `body.happened_at ?? null` directly into the INSERT (falling back to `date('now')` only when omitted entirely) with no format check. `parseSqlDate()` (src/format.ts:322-324) on a non-parseable string returns `NaN`, which `computePipelineMomentum`/`computeWeeklyMomentum`/`medianTimeToOffer` then compare against numeric window bounds — a NaN comparison is always false, so the row is silently dropped from every window rather than erroring. Fix: validate happened_at parses to a real calendar date before insert, matching the enum-style validation already used for interaction `type`.

title: DELETE /api/applications/:id returns 204 even when nothing was deleted
why: Deleting a nonexistent or already-deleted application id reports success identically to a real delete, unlike every sibling mutation route.
detail: `app.post("/api/applications/:id/archive")`, `/pin`, `/unpin`, and `/unarchive` all check `if (!result) return c.json({ error: "not found" }, 404)` after their `RETURNING *` update. The delete route (worker/index.ts:985-988) runs `DELETE FROM applications WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?` and unconditionally returns `c.body(null, 204)` without checking `.run()`'s `meta.changes`, so a stale double-click, a race with another tab's delete, or a typo'd id all look identical to a successful delete to the caller. Fix: check `changes > 0` (or select-before-delete) and return 404 otherwise, for consistency with the other single-row routes.

title: Company relationship map hides a contact whenever its name collides with another contact's
why: Two contacts who happen to share a first/last name at the same company — not unusual ("Alex", "Sam") — cause one of them to silently vanish from the company's contact map instead of appearing as an unlinked node.
detail: `referralLinks` is built from `a.referred_by_name`/`a.contact_name` (display strings, worker-joined from `referred_by_contact_id`/`contact_id`), and `linkedNames = new Set(referralLinks.flatMap(l => [l.from, l.to]))` (line 328-330) then filters `unlinked = contacts.filter(c => !linkedNames.has(c.name))` (line 331) purely by name string. If a second, unrelated contact shares that exact name, `linkedNames.has(c.name)` is true for them too, so they're excluded from `unlinked` even though they never appear in `referralLinks` themselves — they simply disappear from the rendered map. Fix: key by contact id (already available via referred_by_contact_id/contact_id on Application) instead of display name.

title: Companies and contacts can be silently duplicated by name via the manual add form
why: Typing "Acme Corp" twice (a typo, a repeat visit to the form, two people entering the same company) silently creates two rows that then fragment that company's applications, contacts, and history across two disconnected entries with no warning.
detail: `app.post("/api/companies")` and `app.post("/api/contacts")` insert unconditionally off `body.name` with no existing-name lookup. Contrast with the feed's own "add to pipeline" flow (worker/feed.ts:591-605), which explicitly does `SELECT id FROM companies WHERE lower(name) = lower(?) AND user_id = ?` before creating, specifically to avoid this. The manual form is the more commonly used path (every application/company/contact added by hand, not via the feed) and has no equivalent guard. Fix: apply the same case-insensitive existing-name check (with a "looks like an existing company — use it instead?" prompt) to the manual create routes.

title: Inbound email writes into any user's account with no sender verification
why: Anyone who can mail the ingest address can forge a 'Forwarded message / From:' block and have attacker-chosen text logged as an interaction against another user's contact, and flip that contact's outreach_status to 'replied' so a real follow-up stops being prompted.
detail: The `email()` handler (worker/index.ts:2691) ignores `message.to` and passes the raw message to `resolveOriginalSender`, which prefers a `From:` address scraped out of the *quoted body* (worker/forwarded-email.ts:44-62) over the envelope. `logInboundEmail` then looks that address up across ALL tenants (`SELECT ... FROM contacts WHERE lower(email) = ?`, no user scope) and, on a single match, inserts an interaction with the attacker's Subject as `notes` and updates `contacts.outreach_status`. Nothing authenticates the sender, the ingest address is shared rather than per-user, and test/forwarded-email.spec.ts has no forgery case. Fix: give each user a per-account ingest address (or a secret token in the local-part) so the target account is chosen by the address, not by a body match, and require the envelope sender to be the account owner before trusting a body-quoted From.

title: Nightly R2 backup is an unencrypted every-tenant plaintext dump that erasure never touches
why: One leaked R2 credential (or a stray bucket-listing path) hands over every user's CV, salary figures, private notes, contact emails/phones, and live share/calendar tokens at once — and a deleted account stays in those dumps for 14 days.
detail: `runScheduledBackup` calls `buildFullExport` (worker/index.ts:1179), which is `SELECT * FROM <table>` with no user scope over 30 tables including `profile` (share_token, calendar_token, api_key_hash), and writes it as plain JSON into the same `DOCS` bucket that holds user uploads, keeping 14 days. `DELETE /api/account` (worker/index.ts:2533) wipes rows and R2 documents but has no hook into `backups/`, so right-to-erasure is incomplete by up to two weeks. Fix: encrypt the dump before `DOCS.put` (the AES-GCM helpers in worker/ai.ts already exist and a second Worker secret costs nothing), and either put backups in a separate bucket with its own credential or exclude the token/credential columns from the dump.

title: No Strict-Transport-Security header
why: A first visit over http:// (typed hostname, stale bookmark, hostile Wi-Fi) can be stripped to plaintext and the session cookie captured, because nothing tells the browser this origin is HTTPS-only.
detail: The global middleware sets X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and the CSP, but never Strict-Transport-Security, and test/security-headers.spec.ts does not assert it either. wrangler.jsonc deliberately routes every request through the Worker so this middleware is 'one place that decides headers' — which makes the omission the code's, not the zone's. Fix: add `c.header("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains")` beside the others and assert it in security-headers.spec.ts.

title: Irreversible account actions accept a bare session with no re-authentication
why: A session borrowed for thirty seconds on an unlocked laptop destroys the whole account with one request — no password, no 2FA, no confirmation the server can see.
detail: `DELETE /api/account` runs `wipeUserData` plus `DELETE FROM "user"` on nothing but a valid session cookie, and the same is true of `DELETE /api/profile/share-token`, `DELETE /api/profile/calendar-token` and `DELETE /api/profile/api-key`. Better Auth is already configured with email/password and a twoFactor plugin, so the credential to re-check is on hand. CSRF is not the risk here (cookies are SameSite=Lax and these are non-GET), session reuse is. Fix: require a password (or TOTP) re-verification on `DELETE /api/account` specifically — Better Auth's sign-in verification endpoint is enough to gate it.

title: Admin 2FA reset and Better Auth impersonation leave no audit trail
why: An admin can strip another user's second factor, or impersonate them outright, and nothing anywhere records that it happened — on a product whose stated pitch is that privacy is structural.
detail: `POST /api/admin/users/:id/reset-2fa` deletes the target's `twoFactor` row and clears `twoFactorEnabled` with no notification to the user and no log row; the `admin()` plugin enabled in worker/auth.ts:16 also exposes `/api/auth/admin/impersonate-user` by default, which mints a session as any user. Neither writes an admin-action record, and there is no table for one. Fix: add an `admin_actions` audit table written by the custom admin routes, and email the affected user when their second factor is reset — the email transport (worker/email/) is already wired.

title: Dev toolchain pins undici versions with five open advisories
why: CI and every local `wrangler dev` run execute an undici with two high-severity advisories (response desynchronization, cross-user cache disclosure); the deployed Worker is unaffected.
detail: `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 0 vulnerabilities — the production tree is clean. The 5 findings (3 moderate, 2 high) all reach undici 7.0.0-7.28.0 through wrangler -> miniflare and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers. `npm audit fix --force` wants @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers@0.22.0, a major bump. Fix: bump wrangler/miniflare/vitest-pool-workers on a branch and re-run the suite plus `npx wrangler types --check`, which CLAUDE.md already flags as the gate a dependency bump breaks.

title: The ICS feed's company join is not tenant-scoped, unlike every /api join
why: A row carrying a cross-tenant company_id would render another user's company name into an unauthenticated ICS feed — the exact leak the /api joins were hardened against in #445, missing on the one route that needs no session.
detail: All three queries in `/calendar/:token` do `LEFT JOIN companies ON companies.id = applications.company_id` (worker/calendar.ts:199, 210, 225) with no `AND companies.user_id = applications.user_id`, while `GET /api/applications` (worker/index.ts:486) and `GET /api/contacts` (worker/index.ts:371) both carry that clause explicitly as defence in depth. Today `findForeignRef` blocks such a row at write time, so this is a missing second line rather than a live leak — but it is missing on the public surface, not the private one. Fix: add the `AND companies.user_id = applications.user_id` predicate to the three joins.

title: /api/import is an authenticated fetch relay reachable by cross-site navigation
why: A third-party page can top-level-navigate a logged-in user to /api/import?url=..., making the deployment fetch an attacker-chosen URL from Cloudflare's IPs with no rate limit and no user intent.
detail: The route is a GET, so the SameSite=Lax session cookie is sent on a top-level navigation, and Hono's session middleware admits it. `isForbiddenUrl` plus the `global_fetch_strictly_public` compat flag keep the fetch off private space (the hostname-only check is documented and the WHATWG URL parser normalises the decimal/hex/short IPv4 forms, so those are not a bypass), and only parsed metadata is returned — the residual is unattributed outbound traffic and probing. Fix: make the route POST (or require a custom header the client already sends), which SameSite=Lax then blocks cross-site outright.

title: The browser extension keeps the Bearer API key in chrome.storage.sync
why: chrome.storage.sync replicates the key in cleartext to the user's Google account and to every browser profile signed into it, widening a credential that reads the whole pipeline and can create applications.
detail: `options.js` writes `{ baseUrl, apiKey }` with `chrome.storage.sync.set`, and `popup.js` reads it back for `Authorization: Bearer ${apiKey}`. `chrome.storage.local` keeps the key on the one machine that was given it, which matches how the key is issued (shown once, per device). The key itself is fine — 122 bits of CSPRNG, SHA-256 at rest (migrations/0054), no plaintext read path anywhere. Fix: switch both files to `chrome.storage.local`.

title: Two banner conditions for folded rails aren't mutually exclusive
why: Both the 'closed applications are showing' banner and the 'every live stage is folded' banner can render at once
detail: The first banner (line 499) shows whenever the closed rails aren't grouped and at least one is unfolded; the second (line 515) shows whenever all five PIPELINE rails are folded. These conditions are independent, so folding all live stages while any closed rail sits unfolded (the default state) stacks both banners, matching the exact repro recon captured on the live board. Fix by nesting one inside the other's negation, e.g. render the closed-open banner only when `!PIPELINE.every((r) => shownFolded.has(r))`.

title: Board company chip clips mid-word with no ellipsis
why: Text is cut off without a truncation indicator, reading as garbled output
detail: `.bstrip .bco` only sets `min-width: 0` and `flex: 1 1 auto` to let the flex item shrink; it never sets `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`. The comment directly above the markup (board.tsx:115-118) even says the cell 'clips hard,' but the CSS doesn't add the ellipsis that clipping needs. Result: 'SOLACE SYSTEMS · DIE' with a hard word break and no '…'. The `title` attribute is present as a fallback, which masks the bug on hover but not on first glance.

title: Public share page hardcodes its own copy of the pipeline stage order
why: Same stage list maintained twice, one copy untyped, on the most public-facing route in the app
detail: `SHARE_PIPELINE = ["interested", "applied", "screening", "interview", "offer"]` in worker/index.ts is a plain string array duplicating `PIPELINE: Status[]` from src/format.ts verbatim. worker/index.ts already imports `STATUSES as ALL_STATUSES` from `../src/types.js` at line 26, so importing `PIPELINE` from `../src/format.js` the same way is available and would remove both the duplication and the loss of the `Status[]` type on the copy. If the pipeline stages are ever reordered or renamed, this is the one copy nobody will remember to update, and it drives the server-rendered `/shared/:token` funnel chart.

title: shareParseSqlDate is a byte-for-byte copy of parseSqlDate
why: Identical one-line date parser reimplemented under a different name instead of imported
detail: Both functions are `new Date(d.includes("T") ? d : d.replace(" ", "T") + "Z").getTime()`, word for word. worker/index.ts already cross-imports from src/ (see the STATUSES import at line 26), so this is a straightforward dead duplication rather than a build constraint. Not yet drifted, but any future fix to parseSqlDate's known edge cases (see its own comment history around today()/#516) would silently miss the share page's copy.

title: uploadDocument reimplements request()'s error handling and drops the 401/412 special cases
why: A document upload during an expired session shows 'Upload failed (401)' instead of the friendly session-expired message every other API call gets
detail: `request()` special-cases 401 (`errors.sessionExpired`) and 412 (`errors.staleEdit`) before falling through to the generic `(body as {error?:string}).error ?? "Request failed (...)"` shape. `uploadDocument` can't reuse `request()` because it sends a raw file body with a content-type header instead of JSON, so it hand-rolls just the generic branch — silently losing the 401 (and network-error, since there's no try/catch around its `fetch`) handling that every other write path has. A user whose session lapses mid-upload gets a jargon-y numeric error instead of being told to sign in again.

title: Optimistic-concurrency (If-Match/412) check is copy-pasted three times
why: Same ~15-line block (select updated_at, compare header, 412 with current_updated_at) duplicated three times with only the table name and error string varying
detail: Each PUT handler re-fetches `updated_at`, compares it against the `If-Match` header, and returns the same 412 body shape by hand. A small helper like `checkIfMatch(db, table, id, userId, ifMatch, resourceName)` returning either null or a Response would remove ~40 duplicated lines and guarantee the three resources can't drift in status code, header semantics, or body shape the way copy-pasted validation usually does over time.

title: formatComp is dead code
why: Exported function with zero callers anywhere in src/, worker/, or the test suites
detail: `noUnusedLocals` only flags unused locals, not unused exports, so this slipped through tsc. Grepping the whole repo (`grep -rn "formatComp\b"`) finds only the declaration. It duplicates most of what `totalComp`/`totalCompBreakdown` already do for comp display; safe to delete unless it's intended for near-term use, in which case it should be wired in or dropped.

title: totalComp(a) is recomputed 2-3 times per render instead of once
why: Same pure computation called repeatedly in the same JSX subtree with a `!` non-null assertion papering over the redundancy
detail: Both call sites do `totalComp(a) != null ? ... totalComp(a)! ...`, and detail.tsx additionally calls it a third time a few lines later for `diffPct`. The function is cheap today, so this is a readability nit rather than a performance one, but capturing `const comp = totalComp(a)` once would remove the `!` assertions entirely rather than relying on the reader to notice the two calls can't actually disagree.

title: PipelineTab (board.tsx) mixes five independent concerns in one 638-line component
why: Filter/query state, saved-views CRUD, fold/unfold state, and a heavy attention-urgency computation all live inline, making the component hard to change in isolation
detail: Concrete extractions: (1) saved-views state and handlers (`loadViews`/`applyView`/`saveCurrentView`/`deleteView`, lines 941-1006) into a `useSavedViews` hook; (2) fold state and handlers (`folded`/`applyFold`/`openClosedGroup`/`closeClosedGroup`/`unfoldLive`/`toggleFold`, lines 794-866) into a `useBoardFold` hook; (3) the attention/urgency `useMemo` (lines 1019-1097, building `byAppHistory`/`lastActivity`/`gapsByApp`/`gapsByCompany`/`attention`) into a standalone pure function `computeAttention(applications, statusHistory, ...)` outside the component — it takes no React state as input besides `applications`, so it's directly unit-testable once extracted, unlike today where it's only reachable by rendering the tab.

title: ApplicationDetailModal is an 886-line single component with three swappable tab bodies inline
why: The three secTab bodies (track/prep/tailor) are already self-contained JSX blocks delegating to sub-components, making them a clean, low-risk extraction
detail: `secTab === "track"` (784-801: Timeline + Documents), `secTab === "prep"` (803-847: InterviewPrepSection + MockInterview + NegotiationRoleplay), and `secTab === "tailor"` (849-867: JdKeywordMatch + CoverLetterSection) each only need `a`, `onError`, `onChanged`, and `notify` — no other closure state from the 886-line parent. Extracting them to `<DetailTrackTab>`, `<DetailPrepTab>`, `<DetailTailorTab>` would cut the parent by roughly 90 lines and let each tab's own state (e.g. the prep section's internal state) stop living inside one giant function.

title: FeedTab is a 688-line component carrying settings, sort/filter, and band logic together
why: Sort/minFit/showWeak state plus the band-and-sort useMemo (388-420ish) sit in the same component as data loading and item actions
detail: The `visibleItems` useMemo (starting ~406) that sorts, filters by `minFit`, bands by match strength, and re-sorts within band is a pure transform over `items`/`sortBy`/`minFit`/`showWeak` and could be lifted to a standalone `deriveVisibleFeedItems()` next to `sortFilterFeed`/`matchBand` (already free functions elsewhere in the file), leaving FeedTab to own only data loading and event handlers. Lower confidence than the board/detail findings since I didn't trace every closure variable used inside the memo — worth a read-through before extracting.

title: Contacts PUT computes the foreign-key check before the concurrency check but only handles the error after it
why: badRef is computed at line 402, then the whole If-Match block runs (414-431) before the badRef result is finally checked at line 432 — the opposite order from companies/applications PUT, which resolve validation before or interleaved differently
detail: Not a bug (both checks still run and both errors are still returned correctly), but it means an invalid `company_id` reference makes a wasted `SELECT updated_at FROM contacts` If-Match query run before the request is rejected, and the ordering is inconsistent with the applications PUT handler (worker/index.ts:865-870), which checks badRef after the concurrency check but computes it right there rather than pre-computing at the top. Worth aligning so a reader can trust one order across the three near-identical handlers.

title: api.ts request() swallows non-JSON error bodies into a generic message with no logging
why: `res.json().catch(() => ({}))` silently discards parse failures, so a 500 from an edge/proxy layer that returns an HTML error page surfaces only as "Request failed (500)" with nothing in the console to help debug it
detail: This is reasonable user-facing behavior (never show raw HTML to the user) but there's no `console.error` or similar on the caught parse failure, so a misconfigured backend returning non-JSON errors is invisible in the browser console during development. A one-line `console.error` in the catch would preserve the clean user message while keeping the failure debuggable.

title: Backup writes to R2 but there is no restore path anywhere
where: worker/index.ts:2617-2626 (runScheduledBackup); no counterpart found in worker/ or scripts/
why: a backup nobody can load back in is not a backup, it's a write-only cost
detail: runScheduledBackup dumps every EXPORT_TABLES row to a dated JSON key in R2 (backups/YYYY-MM-DD.json) daily at 03:11, but grepping the whole repo for 'restore' turns up nothing — no admin route, no CLI script, no documented manual procedure to load one of these dumps back into D1. If D1 has an incident, corruption, or a bad migration wipes data, the operator has 14 days of JSON sitting in R2 and no supported way to turn it back into rows. Fix is a scripts/restore-backup.mjs (or an admin-only route) that reads a given R2 key and re-inserts rows table-by-table, with a --dry-run count-only mode.

title: Backup success is never verified — a silent write failure looks identical to success
where: worker/index.ts:2617-2626 (runScheduledBackup); worker/index.ts:2669 (independently wrapper only logs via console.error)
why: the only failure signal is a console.error line nobody is paged on
detail: runScheduledBackup does env.DOCS.put(...) and never reads the object back or checks its size/etag; if the JSON.stringify silently truncated (e.g. a pathological row) or the put partially failed, there's no check. Failures are caught by the scheduled() handler's generic `independently()` wrapper, which only does `console.error` into Workers Logs — nothing pages the operator (no email/webhook/alert), and 'no telemetry' in this codebase is about not tracking users, not about refusing operator-facing alerting. Add a read-back size check plus a self-notification (e.g. an admin-facing notification row, or a webhook to the operator's own endpoint) on failure.

title: R2 backup retention math can go wrong if a day's backup is skipped or the clock drifts
why: pruning by count, not by age, silently shortens the safety window on any gap
detail: BACKUP_RETENTION=14 keeps the last 14 *objects* by key-sort, not the last 14 calendar days. If the cron is skipped for a stretch (deploy outage, CF incident) and then catches up, the retention window is still 14 runs, which is fine — but there's no monitoring of gaps, so an operator has no way to know the actual coverage without listing the bucket by hand. Low severity since R2 storage for ~14 small JSON dumps is trivial, but worth a comment/metric on last-backup-age.

title: Migrations auto-apply on every push to main with no pre-migration backup and no rollback
why: a bad migration lands on the production DB before anyone looks at it, with no safety net
detail: deploy.yml runs `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply zenith --remote` unconditionally on push to main, immediately followed by `npm run deploy`. There is no on-demand backup taken immediately before the migration step, no migration dry-run/plan review gate, and D1 migrations are one-directional (no down migrations anywhere in migrations/ — e.g. 0047_drop_feed_items_status.sql drops a column with no reverse file). If a migration partially applies (some DDL statements in a file succeed, one fails), wrangler's migration tracking table may mark it applied or not depending on where it failed, leaving D1 in a state that doesn't match any migration file and blocking the next deploy until someone manually inspects and patches schema state by hand. Adding a pre-deploy `runScheduledBackup`-equivalent snapshot step (or at minimum requiring migrations to be additive/reviewed) would give a rollback anchor.

title: No guard against a destructive migration shipping via the normal PR path
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml (checks job, no migration-content lint); migrations/0047_drop_feed_items_status.sql, 0025_remove_arbeitnow_source.sql as examples of DROP-bearing migrations that shipped fine
why: DROP TABLE/COLUMN and DELETE FROM migrations pass CI exactly like additive ones
detail: CI's `checks` job never inspects the SQL of new migration files — a destructive DROP/DELETE migration merges the same way as an additive CREATE TABLE, gated only by human review. Given main is protected and requires a passing PR, a lightweight CI step that flags (not blocks) any new migration containing DROP/DELETE/ALTER…DROP COLUMN for extra reviewer attention would cost little and catch the highest-blast-radius category of change before it lands next to a backup step that (per the two findings above) may not even be current.

title: Cron 'independently' wrapper logs failures to console only — no operator alerting exists for any of the three triggers
where: worker/index.ts:2660-2669 (the independently() helper used by all scheduled() branches)
why: observability.enabled:true captures request/exception logs, but nobody is watching them
detail: Every scheduled task (backup, weekly digest, stale-posting check, feed pull, notification delivery) is wrapped in `independently()`, which does `ctx.waitUntil(work.catch(err => console.error(...)))`. This is the only failure signal in the whole cron surface. Cloudflare's observability.enabled captures these in Workers Logs, but Workers Logs has no alerting UI, and this repo — correctly, per its own 'no telemetry' rule — has zero user analytics, which the team may be over-applying to mean 'no operator monitoring either.' The gap: if the digest cron throws every Monday for a month, the only way to notice is manually opening the CF dashboard's Logs tab. A cheap fix within the 'no telemetry' constraint: on catch, insert a row into the existing `notifications` table for the admin user (or a dedicated `operational_alerts` table) so a real failure surfaces in-app, which is infra the app already has and touches no third-party analytics.

title: Feed pull fan-out (Adzuna configs + Greenhouse/Ashby boards) is unbounded and one Promise.all — a single invocation could exceed the Workers per-invocation subrequest limit as boards grow
why: every distinct (adzuna location) + every distinct greenhouse/ashby board across ALL users fires one fetch, all in parallel, in one scheduled() invocation, with no cap
detail: refreshFeed builds one job per distinct Adzuna location config plus one per distinct Greenhouse board plus one per distinct Ashby board (aggregated across every user's watched boards, per the comment at worker/feed.ts:8-22) and awaits them all via a single Promise.all — there's no chunking or concurrency cap. Cloudflare Workers enforce a maximum number of simultaneous/total outbound subrequests per invocation; as users add more per-company ATS boards to watch (a feature explicitly designed to scale with user count, worker/feed.ts:60-70), this fan-out grows unbounded and has no ceiling or backpressure. Today (recon: ~2 users, small board list) it's nowhere near a limit; worth a chunked-batch (e.g. 20 at a time) rewrite before the board list grows, since a mid-run subrequest-limit exception would currently abort the whole refreshFeed call (feed_items insert included) rather than degrade gracefully — each individual fetch already has its own try/catch, but the outer Promise.all itself has none.

title: Backup and digest both run a full-table scan across every EXPORT_TABLES / every user daily/weekly — D1 free-tier row-read budget is the real ceiling, not currently close but unmonitored
where: worker/index.ts:1179-1188 (buildFullExport, 27 tables, unfiltered SELECT *), worker/digest.ts:47-70 (per-user correlated subqueries over applications/status_history/interactions)
why: D1's free tier caps rows read/day; both crons scan full tables with no row-count instrumentation to know how close they are
detail: buildFullExport runs `SELECT * FROM {table}` unfiltered for all 27 EXPORT_TABLES every day at 03:11, and generateWeeklyDigest runs three correlated subqueries per user over applications/status_history/interactions every Monday. At the current ~2-user, ~18-application scale this is trivially cheap. Neither path logs or exposes the row counts it touched, so there's no signal for when this stops being cheap as users and history grow — worth a one-line `console.log` of total rows dumped per backup run, cheap insurance against a silent creep toward the D1 daily read cap with no operator visibility.

title: GitHub Actions are pinned to floating major-version tags, not commit SHAs
why: @v4/@v7 tags can be repointed by the action's publisher (or a compromised account) to different code without any change visible in this repo's diff
detail: All actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/github-script@v7 are pinned by mutable tag rather than immutable commit SHA. This is a standard supply-chain hardening gap (same class as the classic 'tj-actions/changed-files' incident), and since deploy.yml runs with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in its environment, a compromised action tag on that specific workflow would have direct production Cloudflare account access. Pinning to SHA (with Dependabot/renovate to bump) is a one-time, low-effort change.

title: CI 'checks' gate has no timeout, so a hung e2e/wrangler dev step blocks the queue instead of failing fast
where: .github/workflows/ci.yml (checks job, no timeout-minutes on the job or steps; e2e step at :35-37 launches Playwright chromium against wrangler dev)
why: default GitHub Actions job timeout is 6 hours — a hung wrangler dev or a stuck Playwright wait_for eats runner minutes for hours before GitHub's own ceiling kills it
detail: Neither ci.yml nor deploy.yml sets `timeout-minutes` at the job or step level, so a hang (e.g. wrangler dev never coming up, a Playwright wait_for that never resolves) runs until GitHub's default 360-minute job cap. A `timeout-minutes: 15` on the checks job (the suite normally finishes in a few minutes per CLAUDE.md's verification list) would fail fast and free the runner instead of silently burning CI minutes for hours on a hang.

title: SELF_HOSTING.md's D1 migration step has no guard against forgetting to swap database_id — a self-hoster who skips step 2 pushes migrations at the upstream author's production DB
where: SELF_HOSTING.md step 2 ("replace the existing database_id"); wrangler.jsonc d1_databases[0].database_id
why: the doc's only safeguard is a sentence telling the reader to remember to do it
detail: wrangler.jsonc ships with the real production database_id (`ca1cf5c8-4d60-4bb6-80dc-89265bd4e9aa`) committed in the repo. SELF_HOSTING.md step 2 tells the reader to replace it, but nothing in the repo enforces that: a self-hoster who runs `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply zenith --remote` against their own Cloudflare account with an API token that (by account scoping) can't reach the upstream DB would just get an auth error and notice — but the actual risk is smaller than 'writes to the wrong DB' and larger than 'confusing failure mode with no clear pointer back to step 2 in the error path.' Worth either a placeholder database_id (e.g. `REPLACE_ME`) that fails loudly and obviously, or a one-line preflight script that checks the configured database_id before migrating.

title: SELF_HOSTING.md documents no restore procedure, consistent with there being none in code
where: SELF_HOSTING.md (entire file — no 'restore' or 'disaster recovery' section); cross-ref worker/index.ts:2617
why: a self-hoster following this doc end-to-end has a backup cron running silently and no idea what to do with its output if D1 ever needs recovering
detail: The self-hosting walkthrough covers create-DB, create-bucket, secrets, migrate, deploy, and keeping up to date, but never mentions that a daily backup lands in the R2 bucket it just had the reader create, nor what to do with it. This should be fixed together with the missing restore path (see the first finding) — once a restore script/route exists, SELF_HOSTING.md needs a short section pointing at it.

title: Weekly digest and feed-pull crons share no lock — a Cloudflare cron retry (documented CF behavior on timeout) can run generateWeeklyDigest or refreshFeed twice concurrently
why: each task is independently idempotent by DB constraint, so a concurrent double-run is wasted work, not a correctness bug — worth noting, not fixing urgently
detail: generateWeeklyDigest dedupes via `ON CONFLICT (user_id, dedup_key) DO NOTHING` and refreshFeed dedupes via `ON CONFLICT (source, external_id) DO NOTHING`, so a duplicate cron invocation (Cloudflare can retry a scheduled event that doesn't return in time) does not corrupt data or double-notify. The design comment at worker/index.ts:2650-2659 shows this was thought through for ordering (stale-posting vs feed pull), but there's no explicit mention of the duplicate-invocation case being covered by these same constraints — worth a one-line comment recording that the ON CONFLICT clauses are also what makes cron retries safe, so a future edit that removes one doesn't silently reintroduce a double-run bug.

title: No self-serve password reset, and the login screen doesn't say who to ask
where: worker/auth.ts:9-11 (emailAndPassword has no sendResetPassword configured); src/Login.tsx (no forgot-password link anywhere); src/locales/en.json:669
why: every forgotten password becomes a direct, unroutable email/DM to the one-person admin, from a user who has no idea how to reach them
detail: Better Auth's emailAndPassword block only sets `enabled: true` — no reset-password email flow is wired up — and the only recovery-adjacent copy on the login card is `login.inviteOnly`: "Accounts are invite-only. Ask your admin for access." That line is about account creation, not password recovery, and it names no admin, no email address, no link. A locked-out user has zero path forward except guessing how to contact someone outside the product entirely. At 200 invited strangers this is the single largest predictable ticket source.

title: Total 2FA lockout (lost device + lost/never-saved backup codes) has no visible recovery path
where: worker/index.ts:2401-2413 (admin-only /api/admin/users/:id/reset-2fa); src/Login.tsx:81-157 (2FA prompt has no help/contact link)
why: a user stuck on the 2FA code screen with no authenticator and no backup codes has no idea the fix is "email the admin" — they just see a form they cannot pass
detail: Backup codes exist and are a good self-serve path (`account.twoFactorBackupCodesHint`), but the app never tells the person what to do if both the authenticator app and the codes are gone — the only fix is an admin hitting a REST endpoint they'd need to know exists. Adding one line under the 2FA code field ("Lost your device and backup codes? Email <admin>") turns an opaque dead end into a one-step self-diagnosis, even though the actual reset still requires the admin.

title: Feed source failures are indistinguishable from "nothing new today"
where: worker/feed.ts fetchAdzuna (~178), fetchGreenhouse (~228), fetchAshby (~272) — all `catch { return []; }`; src/locales/en.json:397 empty.feedNothingNew
why: a mistyped ATS board slug, missing Adzuna credentials, or an upstream outage all render the exact same empty feed as a genuinely quiet day, so the user assumes the feature works and never reports the real defect (or churns silently)
detail: Every fetch to Adzuna/Greenhouse/Ashby swallows its own failure — a non-2xx response, timeout, or thrown error all resolve to an empty array with a bare comment ("best effort per source"). Nothing records that a source failed. `POST /api/feed/ats-boards` (worker/feed.ts:451) also does zero validation on the slug it's given — a typo saves happily and silently returns nothing forever. The UI's only empty state is `feedNothingNew`: "Nothing new. Feed checks automatically every 6 hours, or hit 'Check now'." Per the brief's own framing, empty and broken must not look identical, and today they render pixel-identical.

title: AI key/tailoring failures collapse every error into one message — rate-limited and out-of-credit read as "broken"
where: worker/ai.ts:392 (validateAnthropicKey only checks res.ok); worker/ai.ts:216, 287, 364 (`res.status === 401 ? "...rejected" : "the AI request failed"`)
why: a user whose key is fine but temporarily rate-limited, or who is simply out of Anthropic credit, gets told their key is "rejected" or the request just "failed" — they cannot tell whether to wait, top up, or regenerate a key, so they file a ticket or churn
detail: `validateAnthropicKey` treats any non-2xx from `/v1/models` (401 invalid, 429 rate-limited, 500/529 an Anthropic outage) identically, so saving a perfectly good key during a transient rate limit produces "that API key was rejected by Anthropic" (worker/ai.ts:392) — a user could reasonably conclude the key itself is bad and regenerate it needlessly. At runtime, `callClaudeTailor`/LinkedIn/interview-prep/negotiation all reduce every failure but 401 to the single string "the AI request failed" (e.g. worker/ai.ts:216-219). Anthropic's response body already carries a distinguishable error type (`invalid_request_error`, `rate_limit_error`, `overloaded_error`) that could drive three different, actionable messages instead of one.

title: BYO Claude key has zero cost visibility before or after use
where: src/locales/en.json:707 account.aiKeyHint; src/settings/account.tsx (AI key panel has no usage/cost display)
why: a first-time user with no context on Anthropic pricing pastes in a key not knowing what a CV-tailoring session or a mock interview will cost them on their own bill, and only finds out when a surprise charge shows up
detail: `aiKeyHint` only says the CV and job description "are sent to Anthropic under your key" — nothing about per-call cost, no running total anywhere in the app, no link to Anthropic's pricing/usage dashboard. For a feature that is explicitly BYO-key (someone else's money, not Zenith's), the product gives them no way to reason about cost before or after using it.

title: Deleting a company silently orphans every application linked to it, with no warning
where: migrations/0001_init.sql:15 (`company_id INTEGER REFERENCES companies(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`); src/companies.tsx:431 → src/app-data.ts:163 deleteWithUndo; src/locales/en.json:857 toast.deleted
why: a user tidying up a duplicate/stale company entry gets a generic "Deleted "X"" toast, then later notices applications on their board have lost the company name, with no memory of why and no way to reconnect it
detail: Company delete routes straight into the same generic `deleteWithUndo` used for everything else (6s hide-then-commit, `toast.deleted` = "Deleted \"{{name}}\""). The FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so any application still pointing at that company loses the link permanently once the 6-second window passes — with no count of affected applications shown up front and no distinct copy warning it will happen. A one-line addition ("N applications will lose their company link") before commit would close this without touching the delete pattern itself.

title: Board cards truncate company names mid-word with no ellipsis
where: src/board.tsx (company chip rendering); verified in screenshot board-desktop.png — "SOLACE SYSTEMS · DIE", "FIELDSTONE ANALYTIC", "BRIGHTPATH TALENT P"
why: reads as data corruption or a rendering bug ("why is my company name cut off?") rather than a deliberate space constraint, which is exactly the kind of cosmetic defect that generates a low-value but easy-to-avoid ticket
detail: Multiple company chips on the live board are cut off mid-word with no `text-overflow: ellipsis` or other visual signal that truncation is intentional — "FIELDSTONE ANALYTIC" and "BRIGHTPATH TALENT P" both look like the name was chopped by accident. A `text-overflow: ellipsis; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap` on the chip (plus a `title` attribute for the full name) fixes this in one CSS rule.

title: Board can show two stacked, overlapping "folded" banners at once
where: src/board.tsx:498-524 (`board.closedOpen` block and `board.allLiveFolded` block render independently and their conditions can both be true simultaneously)
why: two banners with two separate "way back" links stacked on top of each other reads as a rendering glitch, prompting a "the board looks broken" ticket even though both messages are individually correct
detail: When every live stage is folded and the closed group isn't collapsed, both `board.closedOpen` ("Closed applications are showing.") and `board.allLiveFolded` ("Every live stage is folded — only closed applications are showing.") render at once, each with its own link (`closeClosedGroup` / `unfoldLive`). The two are near-duplicate statements of the same underlying situation; the second should suppress or fold into the first when both are true.

title: A raw HTTP status code can still reach the user when the server error has no JSON body
why: a Cloudflare edge error (a 522/502 HTML error page, not a JSON response from the Worker) or any future route that forgets to set `.error` on its response surfaces a bare "Request failed (522)" to the user — meaningless to anyone who isn't debugging HTTP
detail: Every current Worker route and the global `onError` handler (worker/index.ts:2555) do consistently return `{ error: "..." }`, so this fallback is mostly dormant today — but it fires unguarded whenever the response isn't valid JSON at all, which is exactly what happens on a Cloudflare-level outage/522 rather than an app-level error. Routing this specific case through the same `errors.unreachable`/`unreachableRead` copy `api.ts` already built for network failure would keep a genuine edge outage from reading as a cryptic app bug.

title: New invited accounts have no forced password change and no email verification step
where: src/settings/admin.tsx:144-215 (AdminInvite — admin types a password directly and hands it to the new user out of band)
why: the admin must personally deliver a working password to every one of 200 people out of band (Slack/email), and any typo in the email field or transcription error in the password is a support ticket with no self-diagnosis available to the invitee
detail: Account creation is entirely admin-typed (name/email/password/role) with no verification email and no "set your own password on first login" step. There's no built-in channel to actually deliver the credential to the invitee — the admin has to do that manually every time — and if the invited user never receives it (wrong email typo'd, message lost), neither side has any way to know except the user asking why they can't log in.

title: Push notification failures collapse permission-denied, registration failure, and network issues into one message
why: a user whose browser silently denied the permission prompt, versus one whose subscribe() call failed for an unrelated reason, gets the identical "check your browser's notification permission" instruction even when permission isn't the actual problem
detail: `subscribe()`'s catch block has no branching on the thrown error at all — a `DOMException` for a denied permission and any other subscribe() failure (e.g. the push service being unreachable, an expired/invalid VAPID key mismatch) both show `pushError`: "Couldn't do that — check your browser's notification permission." On iOS specifically (already a fragile flow per the surrounding comments about gesture-consuming awaits) this is the only diagnostic a user gets.

title: Server silently drops dead push subscriptions with no user-facing signal that push has quietly stopped working
where: worker/push.ts:87-93 (404/410 → `DELETE FROM push_subscriptions`, no notification to the user)
why: a user who granted push once and then stops getting due-follow-up/stale-posting alerts (because their subscription silently expired or was revoked) has no way to notice except missing a follow-up entirely — by the time they'd file a ticket, the damage (a missed follow-up) is already done
detail: When a push endpoint 404s/410s, the server deletes the row with no signal back to the user — the Settings toggle still reflects whatever the browser's local `getSubscription()` returns, which can remain non-null even after the server has forgotten the subscription entirely. A background re-check (comparing browser subscription state against server-known state, or surfacing 'last push delivered' in Settings) would catch this before it costs the user a missed follow-up.

title: Feed triage — step 3 of the daily loop — has no entry point on Today
why: The loop is open, see due, triage feed — but nothing on Today (or anywhere in the chrome) says the feed has new matches.
detail: tileCounts in App.tsx carries counts only for overview and pipeline, so even the wordmark menu shows no feed number; the Today screen never mentions the feed at all. A user only discovers new matches by navigating to Feed on faith (or via a push notification). Steps 1-2 of the daily loop are one glance; step 3 relies on memory. A one-line strip on Today — count, strongest band, tap-through — closes the loop and costs one query over data the feed already computes.

title: "Done" on a follow-up drops both halves of the loop: nothing is logged, nothing is scheduled next
why: The moment the user does the work is the moment the app forgets it and loses the next step.
detail: done() nulls next_action/next_action_at and that is all: no touchpoint lands on the timeline (so response-rate and ghost detection lose the send), and the application immediately joins the "unplanned" pool whose own hero copy warns "Silence is what kills a search". The promise is "never lose a follow-up", yet the primary button on the primary screen manufactures unplanned applications. A follow-through moment after Done — log it as a touchpoint (type inferred from the action text, date today) and offer +3d / +1w / no next step — keeps both, still one tap for the common case, fully undoable like the existing toast.

title: Gone-quiet "Archive" and Next Up "No reply" record the same outcome two different ways
why: Clearing a ghosted role via the Gone Quiet block silently skips the ghosted status, so Insights' ghost rate undercounts.
detail: markNoReply sets status to "ghosted" — its own comment says that writes the status_history row and "the outcome the Insights column asks for". closeOut, one block over, archives with the status unchanged (still applied/screening), so the same real-world event (no reply, giving up) produces pipeline truth on one path and a hole on the other — and the Gone Quiet block is the path the app itself recommends. closeOut should set ghosted before archiving (undo restores both).

title: All navigation hides behind a top-centre menu while the bottom bar's three permanent slots hold none of the daily loop
why: One-handed mobile use pays a top-centre reach plus two taps for every Today-Feed-Board hop; Pinned, a niche filter, owns a permanent thumb slot.
detail: The wordmark menu is the only route to Today, Feed, Network, CV and Insights, and its trigger sits in the hardest one-handed reach zone; the sole always-visible nav shortcut (top-left corner) goes to Pipeline, not to the screen the product promise is built on. Meanwhile the bottom bar — the only chrome in the thumb zone — spends its slots on Pinned (a board filter whose comment history already documents confusing states), Search, and Notifications. Making the bar Today / Search / Feed (with the unseen-match badge) puts the loop under the thumb; Pinned moves to the board toolbar next to the filters it belongs with. The shell.tsx comments themselves disagree about what the third slot should be (lines 126-130 vs 144-148), which suggests this was never fully settled.

title: Logging a touchpoint costs a navigation, a scroll, and a buried three-field form
why: The most frequent write in the daily loop is the hardest one to reach, especially on mobile.
detail: From Today the path is: open the row, land on detail, scroll past facts/notes/JD/tags to the Track tab, then fill type + date + notes. On the 390px detail page the logger sits thousands of pixels down. The Next Up row's own menu offers only snoozes. Add "Log touchpoint" to the row's RowMenu (and the board card's CardMenu) opening the same one-line form in place — type defaulted to email, date to today — so a between-commitments log is two taps.

title: First-run screen offers the same first action under two different nouns
where: overview first-run; src/App.tsx:663-664; src/components/OnboardingChecklist.tsx; locales onboarding.firstJob vs today.addFirst
why: A zero-state user sees "Add your first job" and "Add your first application" stacked on one screen, both opening the same dialog.
detail: OnboardingChecklist renders directly above the untracked hero on overview; the checklist says "job" (onboarding.firstJob), the hero says "application" (today.addFirst), and PRODUCT.md's terminology section picks "application". The duplication also splits the screen's one call to action in two. Pick one noun per PRODUCT.md, and let the hero CTA satisfy the checklist item rather than repeating it ("job" leaks elsewhere too: quickAdd.title, toolbar.addJob, palette.addJob).

title: Onboarding link promises "Load sample data" but delivers a settings page
why: The copy states an action; the click performs a navigation, and the new user must re-find the action on an unfamiliar settings screen.
detail: "Prefer to explore first? Load sample data" is the exact voice the product wants — copy that states what will happen — which makes the bait-and-switch worse. Either load the sample directly behind a one-line confirm, or reword to "Prefer to explore first? Sample data lives in Settings". The direct load is the better fix: this is the moment of lowest user commitment and highest drop-off risk.

title: Board card company strip clips mid-letter with no ellipsis
why: Five of the visible cards truncate the company — "the second thing a job hunter navigates by" per the code's own comment — into gibberish.
detail: .bstrip .bco gets min-width:0 and flex:1 but no overflow/text-overflow/white-space, so the box hard-clips glyphs. The title attribute exists but is mouse-only. Add white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis so the cut is at least announced, and consider dropping the contact name from the strip at narrow column widths.

title: Closed-only board stacks two banners that describe one state
why: "Closed applications are showing" plus "Every live stage is folded — only closed applications are showing" say the same thing twice, with two different escape links.
detail: When the closed group is open and every live stage is folded, both banners render; the all-live-folded one subsumes the other. Two adjacent system messages with two different link verbs ("Fold them away" vs "Back to live") make the user parse which undo they need. Suppress the closed-open banner whenever the all-folded banner shows.

title: Edit/Pin/Archive/Delete live at the extreme foot of a very long detail page
why: Fixing a typo in a title means scrolling past prep checklists and two AI blocks to find Edit.
detail: On mobile the ActionBar sits after facts, salary research, notes, JD, tags, timeline and the full Track/Prep/Tailor stack. These are record-level actions, not page-end conclusions; the record's header is where a user looks for them. Move Edit (or a compact ⋯ holding all four) beside the title, keeping the destructive Delete behind the menu — this also gives the top-of-page stage switcher a peer instead of leaving the header action-less.

title: "Owe a reply" contact rows state a due follow-up but offer no action
why: The list is grouped by obligation ("Owe a reply (5)", "Follow-up due: Aug 2") yet the rows are inert — no done/snooze, unlike the identical semantics on Today.
detail: The grouping does the hard part: it already ranks people by what you owe them. But acting on the debt means opening the contact and finding the timeline. Mirroring Today's row affordances (a Done that logs the touchpoint, a snooze in the menu) would make the People tab a second workable queue instead of a directory. Confidence is "likely" because I judged from the screenshot and grep, not a full read of contacts.tsx.

title: Feed triage buttons change order and emphasis between desktop and mobile
where: feed-desktop.png (Add to pipeline | Keep for later | Dismiss) vs feed-mobile.png (Keep for later | Add to pipeline | Dismiss); src/feed.tsx:1190-1210
why: The primary action leads on desktop but sits mid-row on mobile, so muscle memory built on one surface misfires on the other.
detail: Desktop's detail pane orders Add, Keep, Dismiss with Add primary-styled and first. The mobile card renders Keep for later first and buries the primary in the middle. For a one-handed triage flow the primary should hold a consistent, predictable position (first, matching desktop and the a/s/d key order in the hint). One-line JSX reorder.

title: Settings says "Search started: NOT SET" while Today and Insights assert "Week 29 of your search"
why: Two surfaces disagree about whether the app knows when the search began, which quietly undermines trust in the derived number.
detail: searchWeekNumber falls back to the earliest application date when search_started_at is unset — a sensible default, but it is presented with the same certainty as a configured value while Settings prints NOT SET. Either write the inferred date back as the default (visible and editable in Settings), or soften the copy when inferred ("Week 29 · since your first application").
